title.zh: 卷一百〇二 載記第二 劉聰
title.raw: 卷一百〇二 載記第二 劉聰 Volume 102 Records 2: Liu Cong

sentences.zh: 劉聰

translations.literal: Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 劉聰，字玄明，一名載，元海第四子也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong, courtesy name Xuanming, also called Zai, was the fourth son of Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, whose courtesy name was Xuanming and who was also known as Zai, was the fourth son of Liu Yuan (Yuanhai).

sentences.zh: 母曰張夫人。

translations.literal: His mother was styled Lady Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was known as Lady Zhang.

sentences.zh: 初，聰之在孕也，張氏夢日入懷，寤而以告，元海曰：「此吉徵也，慎勿言。

translations.literal: Initially, when Cong was in the womb, Lady Zhang dreamed that the sun entered her bosom; waking, she told this, and Yuanhai said, "This is an auspicious omen; be careful not to speak of it."
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Cong was still in the womb, Lady Zhang dreamed that the sun entered her breast; when she awoke she told Liu Yuan, who said, "That is a favorable portent—say nothing of it."

sentences.zh: 」十五月而生聰焉，夜有白光之異，形體非常。

translations.literal: " At fifteen months she gave birth to Cong; there was the anomaly of white light by night, and his bodily form was extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " After fifteen months she bore him, and by night an unnatural white light appeared; his physique was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 左耳有一白毫，長二尺餘，甚光澤。

translations.literal: In his left ear was one white hair, more than two chi long, very lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: A white hair more than two chi long grew from his left ear, bright and glossy.

sentences.zh: 幼而聰悟好學，博士朱紀大奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever, perceptive, and fond of learning; the erudite Zhu Ji thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was bright, quick to learn, and eager for study; the academician Zhu Ji considered him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 年十四，究通經史，兼綜百家之言，《孫吳兵法》靡不誦之。

translations.literal: At fourteen he had thoroughly penetrated the Classics and histories and synthesized the teachings of the hundred schools; there was none of the Sun and Wu Art of War he did not recite from memory.
translations.idiomatic: By fourteen he had mastered the canonical texts and histories and surveyed the hundred schools; he knew every line of the Sun and Wu military treatises by heart.

sentences.zh: 工草隸，善屬文，著述懷詩百餘篇、賦頌五十餘篇。

translations.literal: He was skilled in grass and clerical scripts, good at composition; he wrote over a hundred nostalgic poems and more than fifty fu and eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical calligraphy and at literary composition, leaving more than a hundred reflective poems and over fifty fu pieces and encomia.

sentences.zh: 十五習擊刺，猿臂善射，彎弓三百斤，膂力驍捷，冠絕一時。

translations.literal: At fifteen he practiced striking and thrusting; he had long arms like an ape and excelled at archery, could bend a bow of three hundred jin; his strength was fierce and agile, unrivaled in his day.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he trained in swordsmanship; long-armed like an ape, he drew a three-hundred-jin bow and moved with fierce strength and speed—none of his contemporaries could match him.

sentences.zh: 太原王渾見而悅之，謂元海曰：「此兒吾所不能測也。」

translations.literal: Wang Hun of Taiyuan saw him and was pleased, saying to Yuanhai, "This boy is beyond what I can fathom."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun of Taiyuan took to him at once and told Liu Yuan, "This youth is beyond my powers to measure."

sentences.zh: 弱冠游于京師，名士莫不交結，樂廣、張華尤異之也。

translations.literal: At the capping age he traveled to the capital; there was no eminent scholar with whom he did not associate, and Yue Guang and Zhang Hua regarded him with special esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he frequented the capital, befriended every notable in town, and won particular regard from Yue Guang and Zhang Hua.

sentences.zh: 新興太守郭頤辟為主簿，舉良將，入為驍騎別部司馬，累遷右部都尉，善於撫接，五部豪右無不歸之。

translations.literal: Guo Yi, governor of Xinping, summoned him as chief clerk; he was recommended as fit for generalship; he entered service as acting-major of the fierce-cavalry separate command and rose successively to colonel of the right division; he was good at comforting and attaching people, and none of the powerful families of the five divisions failed to rally to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi, governor of Xinping, appointed him chief clerk and nominated him as an outstanding candidate for military office; he became acting-major of an independent fierce-cavalry unit and eventually colonel of the right division. Skilled at winning people over, he drew every powerful clan of the five divisions to his side.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒表為赤沙中郎將。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, memorialized the throne to appoint him General of the Red Sands Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yong of Hejian recommended him for appointment as general of the Red Sands guards.

sentences.zh: 聰以元海在鄴，懼為成都王穎所害，乃亡奔成都王，拜右積弩將軍，參前鋒戰事。

translations.literal: Cong, because Yuanhai was at Ye, feared harm from the Prince of Chengdu, Sima Ying, so he fled to join the Prince of Chengdu and was appointed General of the Right Strong Crossbow, participating in forward operations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liu Yuan was at Ye, Liu Cong feared Prince Sima Ying of Chengdu would kill him, so he fled to Sima Ying's camp and was made general of the right strong crossbow corps, serving on the forward staff.

sentences.zh: 元海為北單于，立為右賢王，隨還右部。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai became Chanyu of the North, [Cong] was established as Right Virtuous King and accompanied him back to the right division.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan became chanyu of the northern Xiongnu, Liu Cong was named right virtuous king and followed him back to the right division.

sentences.zh: 及即大單于位，更拜鹿蠡王。

translations.literal: When [Yuanhai] assumed the great Chanyu position, [Cong] was reassigned as Prince of Luli.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan took the great chanyu title, Liu Cong was promoted to prince of Luli.

sentences.zh: 既殺其兄和，群臣勸即尊位。

translations.literal: After he had killed his elder brother He, the ministers urged him to take the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had killed his elder brother Liu He, his officials pressed him to mount the throne.

sentences.zh: 聰初讓其弟北海王乂，乂與公卿泣涕固請，聰久而許之，曰：「乂及群公正以四海未定，禍難尚殷，貪孤年長故耳。

translations.literal: Cong at first yielded to his younger brother the Prince of Beihai, Yi; Yi and the dukes wept and firmly pressed him; after a long time Cong consented and said, "Yi and the upright ministers only take my senior age as the reason because the four seas are not yet settled and calamities still abound."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong first offered the throne to his younger brother Liu Yi, prince of Beihai; Yi and the senior officials wept and insisted until Liu Cong at length agreed. "Yi and you ministers," he said, "want me only because the realm is unsettled, disaster still rife, and I am the elder."

sentences.zh: 此國家之事，孤敢不祗從。

translations.literal: This is the business of the state; how dare I alone refuse to obey.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns the fate of the state—how could I refuse what reverence demands?"

sentences.zh: 今便欲遠遵魯隱，待乂年長，復子明辟。

translations.literal: Now I wish at once to follow Duke Yin of Lu far off; when Yi has grown older, I shall restore the clear governance to the heir.
translations.idiomatic: For now I mean to follow the example of Duke Yin of Lu: when Yi comes of age, I shall yield the throne and restore him to full authority."

sentences.zh: 」於是以僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元光興。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he unlawfully assumed the imperial title, proclaimed a general amnesty within his borders, and changed the era name to Guangxing.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he seized the imperial title, proclaimed an amnesty throughout his realm, and adopted the reign title Guangxing.

sentences.zh: 尊元海妻單氏曰皇太后，其母張氏為帝太后，乂為皇太弟，領大單于、大司徒，立其妻呼延氏為皇后，封其子粲為河內王，署使持節、撫軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，易河間王，翼彭城王，悝高平王。

translations.literal: He honored Yuanhai's wife Lady Shan as Empress Dowager, his own mother Lady Zhang as Empress Dowager of the Emperor, appointed Yi as imperial younger brother heir, concurrent Grand Chanyu and Grand Tutor, established his wife Lady Huyan as empress, enfeoffed his son Can as Prince of Henan, appointing him bearer of credentials, grand marshal who comforts the army and grand general commanding all military affairs within and without; Yi was Prince of Hejian, Yi Prince of Pengcheng, Kui Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Liu Yuan's widow Lady Shan as empress dowager and his own mother Lady Zhang as dowager empress; he named Liu Yi imperial younger brother and heir apparent, with concurrent titles of grand chanyu and grand tutor; he took Lady Huyan as empress and enfeoffed his son Liu Can as prince of Henan with full credentials as grand marshal who comforts the army and commander of all forces at court and in the field; his sons Yi was prince of Hejian, Yi prince of Pengcheng, and Kui prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遣粲及其征東王彌、龍驤劉曜等率眾四萬，長驅入洛川，遂出轘轅，周旋梁、陳、汝、潁之間，陷壘壁百餘。

translations.literal: He dispatched Can together with his eastern expedition commander Wang Mi, dragon-general Liu Yao, and others leading forty thousand troops to drive deep into the Luo basin, then exit Huanyuan, maneuver among Liang, Chen, Ru, and Ying, and capture over a hundred fortified camps.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Can with Wang Mi, east-conquest commander, Liu Yao, dragon-general, and forty thousand men deep into the Luoyang plain; they passed Huanyuan pass and ranged across Liang, Chen, Ru, and Ying, reducing more than a hundred fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 以其司空劉景為大司馬，左光祿劉殷為大司徒，右光祿王育為大司空。

translations.literal: He appointed his Minister of Works Liu Jing as Grand Marshal, Left Household Liu Yin as Grand Tutor, Right Household Wang Yu as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He named Minister of Works Liu Jing grand marshal, Household Physician of the Left Liu Yin grand tutor, and Household Physician of the Right Wang Yu minister of works.

sentences.zh: 偽太后單氏姿色絕麗，聰蒸焉。

translations.literal: The false Empress Dowager Lady Shan was of surpassing beauty; Cong committed incest with her.
translations.idiomatic: The sham empress dowager Lady Shan was extraordinarily beautiful; Liu Cong forced an illicit liaison with her.

sentences.zh: 單即乂之母也，乂屢以為言，單氏慚恚而死，聰悲悼無已。

translations.literal: Lady Shan was also Yi's mother; Yi remonstrated repeatedly; Lady Shan died of shame and resentment; Cong mourned her endlessly.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shan was Liu Yi's mother; Yi protested again and again until she died of shame and rage. Liu Cong grieved for her without end.

sentences.zh: -{后}-知其故，乂之寵因此漸衰，然猶追念單氏，未便黜廢。

translations.literal: The empress learned the reason; Yi's favor thereby gradually waned, yet [Cong] still remembered Lady Shan and did not immediately demote or discard [Yi].
translations.idiomatic: When the empress learned why, Liu Yi's standing slipped—but Liu Cong still cherished Lady Shan's memory and did not cast Yi aside.

sentences.zh: 又尊母為皇太后。

translations.literal: He further honored his mother as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He then elevated his own mother to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 署其衛尉呼延晏為使持節、前鋒大都督、前軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed his Guard Commander Huyan Yan as bearer of credentials, grand forward commander-in-chief, and grand general of the forward army.
translations.idiomatic: He named his captain of the guard Huyan Yan commander-in-chief of the van with full credentials and grand general of the forward army.

sentences.zh: 配禁兵二萬七千，自宜陽入洛川，命王彌、劉曜及鎮軍石勒進師會之。

translations.literal: He assigned him twenty-seven thousand palace guards to enter the Luo basin from Yiyang, and ordered Wang Mi, Liu Yao, and the stabilizing-general Shi Le to advance and join him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him twenty-seven thousand household troops to strike the Luoyang basin from Yiyang and told Wang Mi, Liu Yao, and stabilizing-general Shi Le to march and link up with him.

sentences.zh: 晏比及河南，王師前後十二敗，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: By the time Yan reached Henan, the imperial armies had been defeated twelve times in succession, with over thirty thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Huyan Yan reached Henan, Jin armies had lost twelve battles in a row and more than thirty thousand men lay dead.

sentences.zh: 彌等未至，晏留輜重于張方故壘，遂寇洛陽，攻陷平昌門，焚東陽、宣陽諸門及諸府寺。

translations.literal: Before Mi and the others arrived, Yan left his baggage train at Zhang Fang's old fort, then raided Luoyang, broke through the Pingchang Gate, and burned the Dongyang, Xuanyang gates and various offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi had not arrived when Huyan Yan parked his baggage at Zhang Fang's old camp, struck Luoyang, broke the Pingchang Gate, and set fire to the Dongyang and Xuanyang gates and government compounds.

sentences.zh: 懷帝遣河南尹劉默距之，王師敗於社門。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai sent Henan governor Liu Mo to oppose him; the imperial army was defeated at the She Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai ordered Henan governor Liu Mo to resist; Jin forces were routed at the She Gate.

sentences.zh: 晏以外繼不至，出自東陽門，掠王公已下子女二百餘人而去。

translations.literal: Because external reinforcements did not arrive, Yan went out through the Dongyang Gate, plundered over two hundred sons and daughters of princes and dukes downward, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When relief failed to come, Huyan Yan rode out the Dongyang Gate, seized more than two hundred sons and daughters of the nobility, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時帝將濟河東遁，具船于洛水，晏盡焚之，還于張方故壘。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was about to flee east across the river; boats had been prepared on the Luo; Yan burned them all and returned to Zhang Fang's old fort.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to slip east across the river; boats waited on the Luo until Huyan Yan burned every hull and fell back to Zhang Fang's old fort.

sentences.zh: 王彌、劉曜至，復與晏會圍洛陽。

translations.literal: When Wang Mi and Liu Yao arrived, they joined Yan again to besiege Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and Liu Yao arrived and joined Huyan Yan to tighten the siege of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時城內饑甚，人皆相食，百官分散，莫有固志。

translations.literal: Famine inside the city was extreme; people ate one another; officials scattered; none had a firm will.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation inside the walls turned men cannibal; officials fled; no one held a steady resolve.

sentences.zh: 宣陽門陷，彌、晏入於南宮，升太極前殿，縱兵大掠，悉收宮人、珍寶。

translations.literal: The Xuanyang Gate fell; Mi and Yan entered the southern palace, ascended the hall before the Taiji Palace, and gave their soldiers free rein to plunder greatly, seizing all palace women and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanyang Gate fell, Wang Mi and Huyan Yan burst into the southern palace, mounted the hall fronting the Taiji sanctuary, and let their troops sack it—every woman of the harem and every treasure was taken.

sentences.zh: 曜於是害諸王公及百官已下三萬餘人，于洛水北築為京觀。

translations.literal: Yao thereupon killed over thirty thousand princes, dukes, and officials downward, and piled their corpses north of the Luo River into a viewing mound.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao then slaughtered more than thirty thousand princes, nobles, and officials, heaping the bodies north of the Luo into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 遷帝及惠帝羊-{后}-、傳國六璽於平陽。

translations.literal: He relocated the emperor, Empress Yang of Emperor Hui, and the six dynastic seals to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the emperor, Empress Yang of Emperor Hui, and the six dynastic jade seals to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 聰大赦，改年嘉平，以帝為特進、左光祿大夫、平阿公。

translations.literal: Cong proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the year to Jiaping, and appointed the emperor as specially advanced, household physician of the left, and Duke of Ping'e.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong declared a general amnesty, adopted the year-name Jiaping, and gave the Jin emperor the titular rank of supernumerary grandee, left household grandee, and duke of Ping'e.

sentences.zh: 遣其平西趙染、安西劉雅率騎二萬攻南陽王模于長安，粲、曜率大眾繼之。

translations.literal: He sent his Pacification-West Zhao Ran and Pacification-West Liu Ya leading twenty thousand horse to attack Prince of Nanyang Mo at Chang'an; Can and Yao followed with a large host.
translations.idiomatic: He sent pacification-generals of the west Zhao Ran and Liu Ya with twenty thousand cavalry against Sima Mo, prince of Nanyang, at Chang'an; Liu Can and Liu Yao brought the main army behind them.

sentences.zh: 染敗王師于潼關，將軍呂毅死之。

translations.literal: Ran defeated the imperial army at Tong Pass; general Lu Yi died in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran beat the Jin host at Tong Pass, where general Lu Yi fell in action.

sentences.zh: 軍至於下邽，模乃降染。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xia gui, Mo then surrendered to Ran.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Xiagui, Sima Mo capitulated to Zhao Ran.

sentences.zh: 染送模於粲，粲害模及其子范陽王黎，送衛將軍梁芬、模長史魯繇、兼散騎常侍杜驁、辛謐及北宮純等於平陽。

translations.literal: Ran sent Mo to Can; Can executed Mo and his son Prince Fanyang Li; he sent Guard-General Liang Fen, Mo's chief clerk Lu Yao, concurrent Cavalier Attendant Du Ao, Xin Mi, and Bei Gongchun and others to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran forwarded Sima Mo to Liu Can, who executed Mo and his son Li, prince of Fanyang, then sent Liang Fen, guard-general, Lu Yao, chief clerk, concurrent cavaliers Du Ao and Xin Mi, Bei Gongchun, and others to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 聰以粲之害模也，大怒。

translations.literal: Cong was furious because Can had killed Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was furious that Liu Can had put Sima Mo to death.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「臣殺模本不以其晚識天命之故，但以其晉氏肺腑，洛陽之難不能死節，天下之惡一也，故誅之。

translations.literal: Can said: "Your servant killed Mo not because he lately recognized Heaven's mandate, but because he was flesh and bone of the Jin house and at Luoyang's crisis could not die for principle—that was one evil under Heaven—therefore I executed him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can replied: "I executed Mo not because he suddenly recognized Heaven's will but because, bone of the Jin imperial clan, he failed to die for honor during Luoyang's catastrophe—one of the worst villains alive—so I removed him."

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「雖然，吾恐汝不免誅降之殃也。

translations.literal: " Cong said: "Even so, I fear you will not escape the misfortune of executing one who had surrendered."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong said: "Even so, I fear you invite the curse that falls on those who kill men who yield."

sentences.zh: 夫天道至神，理無不報。」

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is supremely spiritual; in principle nothing goes unrequited."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is subtle beyond telling; cause never fails of consequence."

sentences.zh: 署劉曜為車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、雍州牧，改封中山王，鎮長安，王彌為大將軍，封齊公。

translations.literal: He appointed Liu Yao as grand chariot-and-cavalry general, commander equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Yongzhou, changed his fief to Prince of Zhongshan, to hold Chang'an; Wang Mi as grand general, fief as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He named Liu Yao grand chariot-and-cavalry general with privilege equal to the Three Excellencies and shepherd of Yongzhou, transferring his title to prince of Zhongshan to garrison Chang'an; Wang Mi became grand general and duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 尋而石勒等殺彌於己吾而並其眾，表彌叛狀。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Le and others killed Mi at Yiwu and absorbed his host; they memorialized Mi's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Le killed Wang Mi at Yiwu, swallowed his army, and memorialized Wang Mi's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，遣使讓勒專害公輔，有無上之心，又恐勒之有二志也，以彌部眾配之。

translations.literal: Cong was greatly angered, sent envoys to reproach Le for on his own harming a minister of state, having a heart disloyal to the sovereign, and also feared Le might have second thoughts, so he assigned Mi's troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong raged: envoys rebuked Shi Le for murdering a pillar minister without orders—treason in intent—and fearing divided loyalty handed Wang Mi's troops to him anyway.

sentences.zh: 劉曜既據長安，安定太守賈疋及諸氐羌皆送質任，唯雍州刺史麹特、新平太守竺恢固守不降。

translations.literal: After Liu Yao had occupied Chang'an, the governor of Anding Jia Yu and various Di and Qiang all sent hostages; only Yongzhou governor Qu Te and Xinping governor Zhu Hui held firm and would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Yao held Chang'an, Jia Yu of Anding and the Di and Qiang tribes all sent hostages; only Yongzhou's Qu Te and Xinping's Zhu Hui held their walls and refused submission.

sentences.zh: 護軍麹允、頻陽令梁肅自京兆南山將奔安定，遇疋任子于陰密，擁還臨涇，推疋為平南將軍，率眾五萬，攻曜于長安，扶風太守梁綜及麹特、竺恢等亦率眾十萬會之。

translations.literal: Protector-General Qu Yun, Pinyang magistrate Liang Su were fleeing from the capital district southern hills toward Anding; they met Yu's eldest son on hostage duty at Yinmi, turned back with him to Linjing, and raised Yu as General Who Pacifies the South; he led fifty thousand to attack Yao at Chang'an; Fufeng governor Liang Zong and Qu Te, Zhu Hui, etc. also led one hundred thousand to join.
translations.idiomatic: Protector Qu Yun and Pinyang magistrate Liang Su fled south from Jingzhao toward Anding, picked up Jia Yu's hostage son at Yinmi, turned toward Linjing, and proclaimed Jia Yu pacifier-general of the south—fifty thousand men marched on Liu Yao at Chang'an while Liang Zong of Fufeng, Qu Te, Zhu Hui, and others brought another hundred thousand to the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 曜遣劉雅、趙染來距，敗績而還。

translations.literal: Yao sent Liu Ya and Zhao Ran to oppose them; they were defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Liu Ya and Zhao Ran to intercept them but suffered defeat and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 曜又盡長安銳卒與諸軍戰于黃丘，曜眾大敗，中流矢，退保甘渠。

translations.literal: Yao again led all Chang'an's crack troops to fight the allied armies at Huangqiu; Yao's host was heavily defeated; he was struck by a flowing arrow and withdrew to defend Ganqu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao committed every elite regiment from Chang'an to Huangqiu, suffered a crushing rout, took an arrow wound himself, and withdrew to Ganqu.

sentences.zh: 杜人王禿、紀特等攻劉粲于新豐，粲還平陽。

translations.literal: Du people Wang Tu, Ji Te and others attacked Liu Can at Xinfeng; Can returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tu and Ji Te of Du county attacked Liu Can at Xinfeng, forcing him back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 曜攻陷池陽，掠萬餘人歸於長安。

translations.literal: Yao captured Chiyang, plundered over ten thousand people, and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao stormed Chiyang, dragged off more than ten thousand captives, and retired to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時閻鼎等奉秦王為皇太子，入于雍城，關中戎晉莫不回應。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Ding and others supported the Prince of Qin as crown prince and entered Yong city; everyone in Guanzhong, Rong and Jin alike, responded.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yan Ding enthroned the prince of Qin as heir apparent at Yong city; every Jin and tribal leader in Guanzhong rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 聰-{后}-呼延氏死，將納其太保劉殷女，其弟乂固諫。

translations.literal: After Cong's empress Lady Huyan died, he was about to take daughters of his Grand Guardian Liu Yin; his younger brother Yi firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Huyan died, Liu Cong planned to take daughters of grand guardian Liu Yin; his brother Liu Yi vehemently opposed it.

sentences.zh: 聰更訪之于太宰劉延年、大傅劉景，景等皆曰：「臣常聞太保自云周劉康公之後，與聖氏本源既殊，納之為允。

translations.literal: Cong consulted again with Grand Preceptor Liu Yannian and Grand Tutor Liu Jing; Jing and others all said: "We have often heard the Grand Guardian say he is descended from the Zhou Duke Liu Kang's line—his source from the sage house is already different; taking them is appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong asked grand preceptor Liu Yannian and grand tutor Liu Jing; Liu Jing said, "The grand guardian claims descent from Duke Kang of Zhou—his bloodline diverges from yours; the marriage is permissible."

sentences.zh: 」聰大悅，使其兼大鴻臚李弘拜殷二女為左右貴嬪，位在昭儀上。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly pleased and had his concurrent grand herald Li Hong invest two of Yin's daughters as left and right noble consorts, rank above the Brilliant Companion.
translations.idiomatic: " Delighted, Liu Cong ordered Li Hong, concurrent grand herald of guests, to install two of Liu Yin's daughters as senior noble concorts outranking the Brilliant Companion.

sentences.zh: 又納殷女孫四人為貴人，位次貴嬪。

translations.literal: He also took four granddaughters of Yin as noble ladies, rank below the noble consorts.
translations.idiomatic: He added four of Liu Yin's granddaughters as noble ladies just below those consorts.

sentences.zh: 謂弘曰：「此女輩皆姿色超世，女德冠時，且太保於朕實自不同，卿意安乎？

translations.literal: He said to Hong: "These women all have beauty surpassing the age and womanly virtue foremost in the time; moreover the Grand Guardian is truly unlike Us—are you at ease in mind?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Hong, "Each of these women is a paragon of beauty and virtue, and the grand guardian's lineage is hardly the same as mine—does that settle your conscience?"

sentences.zh: 」弘曰：「太保胤自有周，與聖源實別，陛下正以姓同為恨耳。

translations.literal: " Hong said: "The Grand Guardian's posterity comes from Zhou itself; his source from the sage house is truly distinct; Your Majesty only regrets the identical surname."
translations.idiomatic: " Li Hong replied, "His house stems from Zhou itself—quite apart from yours—Your Majesty only bridles at sharing the surname Liu."

sentences.zh: 且魏司空東萊王基當世大儒，豈不達禮乎！

translations.literal: Moreover Wei Minister of Works Wang Ji of Donglai was the great scholar of the age—would he not comprehend ritual!
translations.idiomatic: When Wei dynast's minister of works Wang Ji of Donglai, the age's great classicist, took a bride with the same surname, did he flout ritual?

sentences.zh: 為子納司空太原王沈女，以其姓同而源異故也。

translations.literal: For his son he took a daughter of Minister of Works Wang Shen of Taiyuan—because the surname was the same but the origin different.
translations.idiomatic: He married his son to a daughter of minister of works Wang Shen of Taiyuan precisely because the clan name matched yet the descent differed."

sentences.zh: 」聰大悅，賜弘黃金六十斤，曰：「卿當以此意諭吾子弟輩。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly pleased and granted Hong sixty jin of gold, saying: "You must use this meaning to instruct Our sons and younger kin."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong was delighted, gave Li Hong sixty jin of gold, and said, "Explain this reasoning to my sons and brothers."

sentences.zh: 」於是六劉之寵傾于後宮，聰稀復出外，事皆中黃門納奏，左貴嬪決之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the favor of the six Lius tilted the rear palace; Cong rarely went out again; affairs were all submitted through palace eunuchs, and the left noble consort decided them.
translations.idiomatic: " The six Liu ladies now dominated the harem; Liu Cong seldom emerged; eunuchs filed memorials and the senior left consort ruled on them.

sentences.zh: 聰假懷帝儀同三司，封會稽郡公，庾瑉等以次加秩。

translations.literal: Cong granted Emperor Huai credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed him as Duke of Kuaiji commandery; Yu Min and others received ranks in due order.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong gave Emperor Huai honorary parity with the Three Excellencies and the ducal title of Kuaiji; Yu Min and others received stepped promotions.

sentences.zh: 聰引帝入宴，謂帝曰：「卿為豫章王時，朕嘗與王武子相造，武子示朕於卿，卿言聞其名久矣。

translations.literal: Cong brought the emperor in to a banquet and said to him: "When you were Prince of Yuzhang, I once visited with Wang Wuzi; Wuzi showed me to you, and you said you had long heard my name."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong led Emperor Huai into a banquet and said, "When you were prince of Yuzhang, I once called on Wang Yan with Wang Wu zi; he introduced me, and you said you had wanted to meet me for years."

sentences.zh: 以卿所制樂府歌示朕，謂朕曰：'聞君善為辭賦，試為看之。

translations.literal: He showed me the Music Bureau songs you had composed and said to me, 'I hear you are skilled at lyrics and fu—try writing something for me to see.'
translations.idiomatic: You showed me the Music Bureau verses you had composed and said to me, 'They say you excel at lyrics and rhapsodies—write something for me to see.'

sentences.zh: '朕時與武子俱為《盛德頌》，卿稱善者久之。

translations.literal: ' At that time I together with Wuzi both composed 'Ode to Great Virtue'; you praised it at length.
translations.idiomatic: Then you and Wang Yan each presented odes to sublime virtue, and you praised the verses at length.

sentences.zh: 又引朕射於皇堂，朕得十二籌，卿與武子俱得九籌，卿贈朕柘弓、銀研，卿頗憶否？

translations.literal: He also had me shoot in the imperial hall; I scored twelve tallies, you and Wuzi both scored nine; you presented me with a mulberry bow and silver inkstone—do you remember rather clearly?
translations.idiomatic: You took me to the imperial hall for archery: I scored twelve counters while you and Wang Yan each scored nine, and you gave me a mulberry bow and silver inkstone. Do you remember?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「臣安敢忘之，但恨爾日不早識龍顏。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your servant how dare forget—but regrets that on that day he did not sooner recognize the dragon countenance."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Huai replied, "How could I forget—I only regret that I failed then to recognize Your Majesty's dragon bearing."

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「卿家骨肉相殘，何其甚也？

translations.literal: " Cong said: "How greatly has your house's flesh and blood destroyed one another!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong asked, "Why did your own kin tear one another apart so viciously?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此殆非人事，皇天之意也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "This is probably not human affair—it is Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered, "That was scarcely human malice—it was Heaven's design."

sentences.zh: 大漢將應乾受曆，故為陛下自相驅除。

translations.literal: The great Han is about to respond to Qian and receive the calendar; therefore they have been driving one another out for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The great Han is destined to answer Heaven's cycle; that is why my kinsmen destroyed one another to clear the way for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且臣家若能奉武皇之業，九族敦睦，陛下何由得之！

translations.literal: Moreover if your servant's house could have upheld Emperor Wu's enterprise with the nine kin in harmony—how could Your Majesty have obtained it!
translations.idiomatic: Had my clan sustained Emperor Wu's enterprise and kept the nine branches at peace among themselves, how could Your Majesty ever have reached the throne?

sentences.zh: 」至日夕乃出，以小劉貴人賜帝，謂帝曰：「此名公之孫，今特以相妻，卿宜善遇之。

translations.literal: " When evening fell they let him out; he gave the emperor the young noble lady Liu in marriage, saying to him: "She is a granddaughter of a renowned house; now I especially give her to you as wife—you should treat her well."
translations.idiomatic: " At dusk they released him and Liu Cong bestowed the young Lady Liu on him as wife, saying, "She is descended from a great house; I give her to you in marriage—treat her kindly."

sentences.zh: 」拜劉為會稽國夫人。

translations.literal: " Lady Liu was invested as lady of the Kuaiji princedom.
translations.idiomatic: " She was invested as duchess consort of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 遣其鎮北靳沖寇太原，平北卜珝率眾繼之。

translations.literal: He sent his Pacification-North Jin Chong to raid Taiyuan; Pacification-North Bu Xu led troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched pacification-general of the north Jin Chong against Taiyuan while pacification-general of the north Bu Xu followed with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 沖攻太原不克，而歸罪於珝，輒斬之。

translations.literal: Chong attacked Taiyuan without taking it, then blamed Xu and on his own executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chong failed to take Taiyuan, blamed Bu Xu, and executed him on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 聰聞之，大怒曰：「此人朕所不得加刑，沖何人哉！

translations.literal: When Cong heard of it, he raged: "This man I could not punish with execution—who is Chong to do so!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong learned of it he thundered, "Even I could not put that man to death—who is Jin Chong to kill him!"

sentences.zh: 」遣其御史中丞浩衍持節斬沖。

translations.literal: " He sent his palace aide to the censor-in-chief Hao Yan, bearing credentials, to execute Chong.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent chief palace censor Hao Yan with imperial credentials to execute Jin Chong.

sentences.zh: 左都水使者襄陵王攄坐魚蟹不供，將作大匠望都公靳陵坐溫明、徽光二殿不成，皆斬於東市。

translations.literal: The left superintendent of waters Prince Xiangling Yun was sentenced for not supplying fish and crabs; the Grand Master Builder Duke of Wangdu Jin Ling was sentenced for not finishing the Bright Warmth and Radiant Light halls; both were executed at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Yun of Xiangling, left superintendent of waterways, died because fish and crabs were short for the kitchens; Duke Jin Ling of Wangdu, chief builder, died because the Bright Warmth and Radiant Light halls remained unfinished—both were beheaded at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 聰游獵無度，常晨出暮歸，觀漁于汾水，以燭繼晝。

translations.literal: Cong hunted without restraint, often out at dawn and back at dusk; he watched fishing on the Fen River and used candles to continue into daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong hunted without measure, sometimes riding out at dawn and returning after dark; he watched fishermen on the Fen by torchlight long after sunset.

sentences.zh: 中軍王彰諫曰：「今大難未夷，余晉假息，陛下不懼白龍魚服之禍，而昏夜忘歸。

translations.literal: Central Army Wang Zhang remonstrated: "The great disaster is not yet quelled; remnant Jin draws breath—Your Majesty does not fear the misfortune of the white dragon in fish garb, yet forgets return through nightfall."
translations.idiomatic: Central Army commander Wang Zhang urged him: "The great catastrophe is not ended—surviving Jin still draws breath—yet Your Majesty ignores the peril of the dragon disguised as a fish and wanders until midnight without returning."

sentences.zh: 陛下當思先帝創業之艱難，嗣承之不易，鴻業已爾，四海屬情，何可墜之于垂成，隳之於將就！

translations.literal: Your Majesty should ponder how hard the late emperor's founding was and how hard succession is—the great enterprise is already thus; the four seas lean on you—how can you let it fall when nearly complete, ruin it when almost done!
translations.idiomatic: Remember the toil of the founding fathers and the fragility of the line you now hold: the realm already leans on you—how can you shatter it on the very verge of success or waste it at the moment of consummation!

sentences.zh: 比竊觀陛下所為，臣實痛心疾首有日矣。

translations.literal: Lately I have spied on what Your Majesty does; your servant has been heartsick and tearing his hair for many days.
translations.idiomatic: I have watched what Your Majesty does, and for many days my heart has burned with anguish.

sentences.zh: 且愚人系漢之心未專，而思晉之懷猶盛，劉琨去此咫尺之間，狂狷刺客息頃而至。

translations.literal: Moreover the foolish people's attachment to Han is not yet single-minded, while longing for Jin still runs strong; Liu Kun is within a stone's throw; reckless assassins can arrive in a breath.
translations.idiomatic: The common folk are not yet devoted solely to Han; their hunger for the old Jin is still keen. Liu Kun is a short ride away, and a desperate blade can reach you in a moment.

sentences.zh: 帝王輕出，一夫敵耳。

translations.literal: When an emperor lightly goes abroad, a single common foe is enough.
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor wanders lightly abroad, any lone assassin may strike him down.

sentences.zh: 願陛下改往修來，則憶兆幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to mend past errors and cultivate the future—then the myriad millions will be supremely fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty amends past faults and builds anew, the myriad subjects will count themselves blessed beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」聰大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: " Cong was greatly angered and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong flew into a rage and ordered Wang Zhang executed.

sentences.zh: 上夫人王氏叩頭乞哀，乃囚之詔獄。

translations.literal: Lady Wang the honored consort kowtowed and begged for mercy; [Cong] then imprisoned him in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Senior lady Wang kowtowed until her forehead bled; Liu Cong relented enough to jail Wang Zhang in the imperial prison instead.

sentences.zh: 聰母以聰刑怒過差，三日不食，弟乂、子粲並與切諫。

translations.literal: Cong's mother, because Cong's punishments were excessive in anger, fasted three days; younger brother Yi and son Can together urgently remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong's mother fasted three days to protest his cruel judgments; his brother Liu Yi and son Liu Can joined in urgent pleas.

sentences.zh: 聰怒曰：「吾豈桀、紂、幽、厲乎，而汝等生來哭人！

translations.literal: Cong raged: "Am I Jie, Zhou, You, or Li—that you lot were born to cry at people!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong snarled, "Do I look like Jie, Zhou, King You, or King Li—that you were born only to weep at me!"

sentences.zh: 」其太宰劉延年及諸公卿列侯百有餘人，皆免冠涕泣固諫曰：「光文皇帝以聖武膺期，創建鴻祚，而六合未一，夙世升遐。

translations.literal: " His Grand Preceptor Liu Yannian and the dukes and ministers in column, over a hundred, all removed their caps and wept, firmly remonstrating: "Emperor Guangwen in sage martial virtue received the mandate and founded the great fortune, yet the six directions were not one and he ascended early to the far shore."
translations.idiomatic: " Grand preceptor Liu Yannian and more than a hundred dukes and ministers shed their caps and wept as they pressed him: "Emperor Guangwen answered Heaven's call in sacred might and laid the foundations of our fortune, yet the realm was still divided when he passed away untimely."

sentences.zh: 陛下睿德自天，龍飛紹統，東平洛邑，南定長安，真可謂功高周成，德超夏啟。

translations.literal: Your Majesty by sagely virtue from Heaven, dragon-flight succeeding the line, east pacified Luoyi, south settled Chang'an—truly one may say merit surpasses the Zhou regents, virtue exceeds Xia Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty drew sagely virtue from Heaven, ascended the throne as heir to the mandate, pacified Luoyi in the east and Chang'an in the south—one might truly say your merit rivals the age of King Cheng of Zhou and your virtue surpasses Lord Qi of Xia.

sentences.zh: 往也唐虞，今則陛下，曆觀書記，未有此比。

translations.literal: In former times there were Tang and Yu; now there is Your Majesty. Looking through written records, there has never been such a parallel.
translations.idiomatic: The age of Tang and Yao lies in the past; today we have Your Majesty. Nowhere in the annals is there a ruler who matches this achievement.

sentences.zh: 而頃頻以小務不供而斬王公，直言忤旨，便囚大將，游獵無度，機管不修，臣等竊所未解，臣等所以破肝糜胃忘寢與食者也。

translations.literal: Yet lately you repeatedly execute princes and dukes over petty failures of supply; plain speech that offends the intent brings imprisonment for great generals; hunting knows no limit; government goes untended—we Your servants privately fail to understand this; it is why we tear our livers and grind our stomachs, forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of late you have put princes and dukes to death for trifling shortages, jailed a commander for frank counsel, hunted without restraint, and neglected the machinery of rule—we cannot fathom it, and it is why we ruin our health and forget to eat or sleep.

sentences.zh: 」聰乃赦彰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Cong pardoned Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong then pardoned Wang Zhang.

sentences.zh: 麹特等圍長安，劉曜連戰敗績，乃驅掠士女八萬餘口退還平陽，因攻司徒傅祗於三渚，使其右將軍劉參攻郭默於懷城。

translations.literal: Qu Te and others besieged Chang'an; Liu Yao suffered defeat in successive battles, then drove off over eighty thousand men and women as captives and withdrew to Pingyang; he thereupon attacked Minister of Education Fu Di at Sanzhu and sent his General of the Right Liu Shen against Guo Mo at Huai city.
translations.idiomatic: While Qu Te besieged Chang'an, Liu Yao lost battle after battle, so he dragged off more than eighty thousand civilians and fell back to Pingyang; he then struck Minister Fu Di at Sanzhu and ordered General Liu Shen to attack Guo Mo at Huai.

sentences.zh: 祗病卒，城陷，遷祗孫純、粹並二萬餘戶於平陽縣。

translations.literal: Di died of illness; the city fell; [Yao] relocated Di's grandsons Chun and Cui together with over twenty thousand households to Pingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Di died before the walls fell; Liu Yao moved Fu's grandsons Chun and Cui plus more than twenty thousand households into Pingyang county.

sentences.zh: 聰贈祗太保，純、粹皆給事中，謂祗子暢曰：「尊公雖不達天命，然各忠其主，吾亦有以亮之。

translations.literal: Cong posthumously invested Di as Grand Guardian; Chun and Cui were both made palace attendants; he said to Di's son Chang: "Though your honored father did not comprehend Heaven's mandate, still each was loyal to his lord—I have grounds to forgive him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong posthumously named Fu Di grand guardian, appointed Chun and Cui as palace gentlemen, and told Fu Chang: "Your father never accepted Heaven's verdict, yet each man served his own lord—I can respect that."

sentences.zh: 但晉主已降，天命非人所支，而虔劉南鄙，沮亂邊萌，此其罪也。

translations.literal: But the Jin ruler has already surrendered; Heaven's mandate is not something men can prop up—yet you slaughter the southern marches and shake the border peoples—this is their crime.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor has yielded; no man can shore up a mandate Heaven has withdrawn—yet you ravage the southern frontier and terrorize the border folk. That is their offense.

sentences.zh: 以元惡之種而贈同勳舊，逆臣之孫荷榮禁闥，卿知皇漢之德弘曠以不？

translations.literal: You treat the offspring of chief villains with gifts equal to meritorious elders; the grandsons of traitorous ministers bear honor inside the forbidden gates—do you grasp how vast and magnanimous the virtue of imperial Han is?"
translations.idiomatic: You ennoble the seed of arch-traitors like founding ministers and let rebels' grandsons shine within the palace—do you see how broad our Han virtue runs?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「陛下每嘉先臣，不以小臣之故而虧其忠節，及是恩也，自是明主伐國吊人之義，臣輒同萬物，未敢謝生於自然。」

translations.literal: " Chang said: "Your Majesty always praises my late father and does not, because of your servant's low station, impair his loyal integrity—this reaches to kindness; this is indeed the righteousness of an enlightened ruler who attacks a state yet pities its people—your servant thereby joins the myriad things and does not dare decline life from what is natural."
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Chang answered, "You honor my late father and do not let my low rank diminish his loyalty—that is grace itself. This is what it means for an enlightened conqueror to pity a fallen people. I accept my lot among living things and would not refuse the life Heaven grants."

sentences.zh: 聰遣劉粲、劉曜等攻劉琨于晉陽，琨使張喬距之，戰于武灌，喬敗績，死之，晉陽危懼。

translations.literal: Cong dispatched Liu Can, Liu Yao, and others to attack Liu Kun at Jinyang; Kun sent Zhang Qiao to oppose him; they fought at Wuguan; Qiao was routed and died; Jinyang was in peril and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sent Liu Can and Liu Yao against Liu Kun at Jinyang; Liu Kun posted Zhang Qiao to hold them off at Wuguan, where Zhang was crushed and killed, leaving Jinyang trembling.

sentences.zh: 太原太守高喬、琨別駕郝聿以晉陽降粲。

translations.literal: Taiyuan governor Gao Qiao and Kun's aide Hao Yu surrendered Jinyang to Can.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan governor Gao Qiao and Liu Kun's aide Hao Yu handed Jinyang to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 琨與左右數十騎，攜其妻子奔于趙郡之亭頭，遂如常山。

translations.literal: Kun with several dozen mounted followers, taking his wife and children, fled to Tingtou in Zhao commandery, then went on to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun fled with a few dozen horsemen, his family beside him, to Tingtou in Zhao commandery, then pressed on toward Changshan.

sentences.zh: 粲、曜入于晉陽。

translations.literal: Can and Yao entered Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can and Liu Yao marched into Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，琨與代王猗盧結為兄弟，乃告敗于猗盧，且乞師。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kun and the Prince of Dai Yilu had sworn brotherhood; he now reported his defeat to Yilu and begged for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun had earlier sworn brotherhood with Tuoba Yilu, prince of Dai; he now reported his rout and asked for an army.

sentences.zh: 猗盧遣子日利孫、賓六須及將軍衛雄、姬澹等率眾數萬攻晉陽，琨收散卒千餘為之鄉導，猗盧率眾六萬至於狼猛。

translations.literal: Yilu sent his son Rilisun, Bin Liuxu, and generals Wei Xiong, Ji Dan, and others leading several tens of thousands to attack Jinyang; Kun gathered over a thousand scattered soldiers to guide them; Yilu led sixty thousand troops to Langmeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu sent his sons Rilisun and Bin Liuxu with generals Wei Xiong and Ji Dan and tens of thousands of men against Jinyang; Liu Kun scraped together a thousand survivors as guides while Yilu brought sixty thousand warriors to Langmeng.

sentences.zh: 曜及賓六須戰於汾東，曜墜馬，中流矢，身被七創。

translations.literal: Yao and Bin Liuxu fought east of the Fen; Yao fell from his horse, was struck by a flowing arrow, and received seven wounds on his body.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Fen, Liu Yao and Bin Liuxu clashed; Liu Yao was thrown from his saddle, pierced by an arrow, and suffered seven wounds.

sentences.zh: 討虜傅武以馬授曜，曜曰：「當今危亡之極，人各思免。

translations.literal: Punitive-general Fu Wu gave his horse to Yao; Yao said: "In the present extremity of peril and ruin, each man thinks only of escape."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Wu, colonel who smashes barbarians, offered his mount; Liu Yao said, "We stand at the brink of ruin—every man thinks only of saving himself."

sentences.zh: 吾創已重，自分死此矣。

translations.literal: My wounds are already grave; I reckon I shall die here.
translations.idiomatic: My wounds are mortal—I expect to die on this field.

sentences.zh: 」武泣曰：「武小人，蒙大王識拔，以至於是，常思效命，今其時矣。

translations.literal: " Wu wept and said: "Wu is a petty man who received the Great King's recognition and elevation to reach this point; I have always thought to repay with my life—now is the hour."
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Wu wept, "I am a nobody whom Your Highness raised from nothing—I have long wished to repay you with my life, and the moment has come."

sentences.zh: 且皇室始基，大難未弭，天下何可一日無大王也。

translations.literal: Moreover the imperial house has only begun its foundation; the great disaster is not yet ended—how can the realm go a single day without the Great King!
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's foundations are fresh and calamity still looms—how can the realm endure a single day without you!

sentences.zh: 」於是扶曜乘馬，驅令渡汾，回而戰死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they helped Yao onto the horse, drove him to cross the Fen, then turned back and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: " They lifted Liu Yao onto the horse, spurred it across the Fen, then wheeled about and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 曜入晉陽，夜與劉粲等掠百姓，逾蒙山遁歸。

translations.literal: Yao entered Jinyang; by night he and Liu Can and others plundered the common people, crossed Meng Mountain, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao slipped into Jinyang, joined Liu Can that night in looting the populace, crossed Meng Mountain, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 猗盧率騎追之，戰于藍穀，粲敗績，斬其征虜邢延，獲其鎮北劉豐。

translations.literal: Yilu led horse in pursuit; they fought at Lan Valley; Can was routed; they beheaded his punitive-general Xing Yan and captured his Pacification-North Liu Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu chased them with cavalry, fought at Lan Valley, shattered Liu Can's army, killed general Xing Yan, and took Liu Feng, pacifier of the north.

sentences.zh: 琨收合離散，保于陽曲，猗盧戍之而還。

translations.literal: Kun gathered the scattered and held Yangqu; Yilu garrisoned it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun rallied his broken forces and held Yangqu while Yilu left a garrison and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 正旦，聰宴於光極前殿，逼帝行酒，光祿大夫庾瑉、王俊等起而大哭，聰惡之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day Cong feasted in the hall before the Guangji Palace and forced the emperor to circulate wine; Household Grandee Yu Min, Wang Jun, and others rose and wept aloud greatly; Cong hated it.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's morning Liu Cong held court in the Guangji hall and made Emperor Huai pour wine for his guests; Yu Min, Wang Jun, and others stood up wailing—Liu Cong took offense.

sentences.zh: 會有告瑉等謀以平陽應劉琨者，聰遂鴆帝而誅瑉、俊，復以賜帝劉夫人為貴人，大赦境內殊死已下。

translations.literal: It happened that someone reported Min and others plotted to respond to Liu Kun from Pingyang; Cong thereupon poisoned the emperor and executed Min and Jun; he again took Lady Liu, whom he had given the emperor, as noble lady; proclaimed a general amnesty within his borders for crimes below capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: When informants accused Yu Min and others of plotting to open Pingyang to Liu Kun, Liu Cong poisoned Emperor Huai and executed Yu Min and Wang Jun; he reclaimed Lady Liu—once gifted to the emperor—as his own concubine and granted amnesty short of capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 立左貴嬪劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He established Left Noble Consort Lady Liu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated left noble consort Lady Liu to empress.

sentences.zh: 聰將為劉氏起皇儀樓於後庭，廷尉陳元達諫曰：「臣聞古之聖王愛國如家，故皇天亦祐之如子。

translations.literal: Cong was about to raise for Lady Liu a Tower of Imperial Ceremony in the rear palace; Minister of Justice Chen Yuanda remonstrated: "Your servant has heard that the sage kings of antiquity loved the state as they did their families; therefore August Heaven aided them as sons."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong planned a Tower of Imperial Ceremony in the inner palace for Empress Liu; Minister of Justice Chen Yuanda urged him: "The sage kings of old loved the realm as their own household; Heaven therefore sheltered them like sons."

sentences.zh: 夫天生蒸民而樹之君者，使為之父母以刑賞之，不欲使殿屎黎元而蕩逸一人。

translations.literal: Heaven gave birth to the multitude and set up rulers for them, making them fathers and mothers to apply punishments and rewards; it did not desire to make the groaning black-haired masses suffer while one man roamed in dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven bred the people and set rulers over them as parents—to wield reward and punishment—not to leave the folk groaning in misery while one man indulges himself.

sentences.zh: 晉氏暗虐，視百姓如草芥，故上天剿絕其祚。

translations.literal: The Jin house was dark and cruel, treating the hundred surnames like weeds; therefore High Heaven extirpated their mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court was blind and cruel; it treated the people as straw—so Heaven cut their mandate short.

sentences.zh: 乃眷皇漢，蒼生引領息肩，懷更蘇之望有日矣。

translations.literal: Then it turned to imperial Han; the black-haired masses crane their necks and ease their shoulders, cherishing hope of revival day after day.
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven turned to our Han: the people crane their necks for relief, longing each day for renewal.

sentences.zh: 我高祖光文皇帝靖言惟茲，痛心疾首，故身衣大布，居不重茵；

translations.literal: Our High Ancestor Emperor Guangwen in respectful words pondered only this; he was heartsick and tore his hair—therefore he wore coarse hemp himself and did not double his mats when seated;
translations.idiomatic: Our revered Emperor Guangwen pondered these words with wrung heart—so he wore plain cloth and refused double mats;

sentences.zh: 先皇后嬪服無綺彩。

translations.literal: The former empress and consorts wore no patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: his late consorts wore no figured silk.

sentences.zh: 重逆群臣之請，故建南北宮焉。

translations.literal: Repeatedly violating the requests of the ministers, therefore he built the southern and northern palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Only because he repeatedly yielded to his ministers did he erect the southern and northern palaces.

sentences.zh: 今光極之前足以朝群后、饗萬國矣，昭德、溫明已後足可以容六宮、列十二等矣。

translations.literal: Now before the Guangji Palace is enough to court the host of lords and feast the myriad states; beyond Zhaode and Bright Warmth is enough to house the six palaces and array the twelve ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The space before Guangji hall already suffices to hold court for lords and host tribute missions; beyond the Zhaode and Bright Warmth halls there is already room for the six palaces and twelve ranks of ladies.

sentences.zh: 陛下龍興已來，外殄二京不世之寇，內興殿觀四十餘所，重之以饑饉疾疫，死亡相屬，兵疲於外，人怨於內，為之父母固若是乎！

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty's dragon ascent, outwardly you have extinguished the unprecedented bandits of the two capitals; inwardly you have raised over forty halls and towers—compounded by famine and plague, deaths succeeding one another, troops weary abroad and resentment within—is this indeed how fathers and mothers of the people behave!
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty rose, you have crushed the hosts at the two capitals abroad while raising more than forty palace halls at home—on top of famine and plague, corpses lining the roads, armies exhausted outside and hatred boiling within. Is this how parents of the people ought to act?

sentences.zh: 伏聞詔旨，將營皇儀，中宮新立，誠臣等樂為子來者也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard the edict's intent: you will build the imperial ceremony tower; the inner palace is newly established—truly your servants would gladly come like sons.
translations.idiomatic: We hear you mean to raise the Tower of Imperial Ceremony now that a new empress sits—we would gladly flock to serve like willing sons.

sentences.zh: 竊以大難未夷，宮宇粗給，今之所營，尤實非宜。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers the great disaster not yet pacified; palace buildings are barely adequate—what you now propose to build is truly inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet catastrophe is not ended and palace space barely suffices—this new project is singularly ill-timed.

sentences.zh: 臣聞太宗承高祖之業，惠呂息役之後，以四海之富，天下之殷，尚以百金之費而輟露臺，歷代垂美，為不朽之跡。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Grand Ancestor Wendi inherited Grand Ancestor Gaozu's enterprise; after the troubles of Hui and Lü had ceased labor service, though he had the wealth of the four seas and the abundance of the realm, still over the expense of a hundred jin of gold he halted the Open Terrace—by successive generations praised as an imperishable deed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han inherited Gaozu's work after Empress Lü's tyranny ended; though the empire overflowed with wealth, he refused a terrace that would cost a hundred catties of gold—history still praises that restraint.

sentences.zh: 故能斷獄四百，擬于成康。

translations.literal: Therefore he could settle lawsuits at four hundred—comparable to Cheng and Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus lawsuits dwindled to a mere four hundred cases—a reign likened to Kings Cheng and Kang of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 陛下之所有，不過太宗二郡地耳，戰守之備者，豈僅匈奴、南越而已哉！

translations.literal: What Your Majesty possesses is no more than the territory of Grand Ancestor Wendi's two commanderies; preparations for war and defense—are they merely against the Xiongnu and Southern Yue!
translations.idiomatic: Your realm is scarcely larger than two commanderies of Emperor Wen's Han; you must guard against far more than the old Xiongnu or Nanyue!

sentences.zh: 孝文之廣，思費如彼；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen's breadth—his thought of expense was like that;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ruled a vast realm yet weighed every expense;

sentences.zh: 陛下之狹，欲損如此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's narrowness—yet you desire to cut expenses like this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules a narrow domain yet would lavish resources so recklessly.

sentences.zh: 愚臣所以敢昧死犯顏色，冒不測之禍者也。

translations.literal: This is why your foolish servant dares to risk death and offend your expression, braving unforeseeable disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That is why this foolish minister risks execution to speak bluntly to your face.

sentences.zh: 」聰大怒曰：「吾為萬機主，將營一殿，豈問汝鼠子乎！

translations.literal: " Cong raged greatly and said: "I am master of the myriad threads of rule; I am about to build one hall—must I consult you ratlings!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong exploded: "I rule all affairs of state—may I not raise one hall without mice like you squeaking at me!"

sentences.zh: 不殺此奴，沮亂朕心，朕殿何當得成邪！

translations.literal: If I do not kill this slave, he obstructs and disorders Our heart—when shall Our hall ever be completed!
translations.idiomatic: Unless I kill this slave he will poison my resolve—how will my hall ever rise!

sentences.zh: 將出斬之，並其妻子同梟東市，使群鼠共穴。

translations.literal: He was about to take him out and behead him, together with his wife and children expose them together at the eastern market, and let the pack of rats share one hole.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Chen Yuanda dragged out for execution with wife and children, their heads spiked at the eastern market—let the rats share one burrow.

sentences.zh: 」時在逍遙園李中堂，元達抱堂下樹叫曰：「臣所言者，社稷之計也，而陛下殺臣。

translations.literal: " At the time he was in the Free Roaming Garden, Li middle hall; Yuanda hugged a tree below the hall and cried: "What your servant spoke of was a plan for altars of soil and grain; yet Your Majesty kills your servant."
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong was in his Pleasure Garden's plum pavilion when Chen Yuanda wrapped his arms around a courtyard tree and shouted, "I spoke for the altars of state—and you would kill me for it!"

sentences.zh: 若死者有知，臣要當上訴陛下于天，下訴陛下于先帝。

translations.literal: If the dead have awareness, your servant will surely above appeal Your Majesty to Heaven, below appeal Your Majesty to the former emperors.
translations.idiomatic: If the dead can speak, I will indict you before Heaven and our late emperors below!

sentences.zh: 朱雲有云：『臣得與龍逢、比干游於地下足矣。

translations.literal: Zhu Yun had a saying: 'Your servant would be content to roam in the underworld with Long Feng and Bigan.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yun said he would gladly walk the underworld with Long Feng and Bigan—

sentences.zh: 』未審陛下何如主耳！

translations.literal: ' I do not yet know what sort of ruler Your Majesty is!'
translations.idiomatic: —and then I would know what sort of ruler you are.

sentences.zh: 」元達先鎖腰而入，及至，即以鎖繞樹，左右曳之不能動。

translations.literal: " Yuanda had earlier entered with his waist in fetters; when he arrived, he immediately wound the fetters around the tree; attendants pulled him but could not move him.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Yuanda had entered already shackled; at the tree he looped his chains around the trunk so tightly that guards could not drag him away.

sentences.zh: 聰怒甚。

translations.literal: Cong was extremely angry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was beside himself.

sentences.zh: 劉氏時在後堂，聞之，密遣中常侍私敕左右停刑，於是手疏切諫，聰乃解，引元達而謝之，易逍遙園為納賢園，李中堂為愧賢堂。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was at that time in the rear hall; hearing this, she secretly sent a regular attendant privately to order the attendants to halt the execution; thereupon she personally wrote a sharp remonstrance; Cong then relented, led Yuanda in and apologized to him, changed Free Roaming Garden to Garden for Receiving Worthies, Li middle hall to Hall Ashamed before Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu, in the inner quarters, heard everything; she quietly ordered eunuchs to stay the execution and wrote an urgent plea that softened Liu Cong. He led Chen Yuanda inside, apologized, and renamed the Pleasure Garden the Garden for Welcoming Worthies and the plum pavilion the Hall of Shame before Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時湣帝即位于長安，聰遣劉曜及司隸喬智明、武牙李景年等寇長安，命趙染率眾赴之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Min had assumed the throne at Chang'an; Cong dispatched Liu Yao and Metropolitan Governor Qiao Zhiming, Military Inspector Li Jingnian, and others to raid Chang'an, and ordered Zhao Ran to lead troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min took the throne at Chang'an, Liu Cong sent Liu Yao, capital intendant Qiao Zhiming, and military adjutant Li Jingnian against the city and told Zhao Ran to bring reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時大都督麹允據黃白城，累為曜、染所敗。

translations.literal: At that time grand commander Qu Yun held White-Yellow city and was repeatedly defeated by Yao and Ran.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun, commander-in-chief, held the Yellow-White citadel but Liu Yao and Zhao Ran beat him again and again.

sentences.zh: 染謂曜曰：「麹允率大眾在外，長安可襲而取之。

translations.literal: Ran said to Yao: "Qu Yun leads a large host outside—Chang'an can be taken by surprise."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran told Liu Yao, "Qu Yun's main army is abroad—you can seize Chang'an by surprise."

sentences.zh: 得長安，黃白城自服。

translations.literal: Once Chang'an is taken, White-Yellow city will submit of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Take Chang'an and the Yellow-White fort will surrender on its own.

sentences.zh: 願大王以重眾守此，染請輕騎襲之。

translations.literal: I beg the Great King to hold here with heavy troops; Ran requests light horse to raid it.
translations.idiomatic: Leave your heavy troops here, Great King—I will raid Chang'an with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 」曜乃承制加染前鋒大都督、安南大將軍，以精騎五千配之而進。

translations.literal: " Yao then under delegated authority promoted Ran to grand forward commander-in-chief and grand general who pacifies the south, assigned him five thousand picked horse, and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Yao thereupon, acting under imperial commission, named Zhao Ran grand commander of the van and grand general who pacifies the south, gave him five thousand elite horsemen, and sent him forward.

sentences.zh: 王師敗于渭陽，將軍王廣死之。

translations.literal: The imperial army was defeated at Weiyang; general Wang Guang died there.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops lost at Weiyang; general Wang Guang fell.

sentences.zh: 染夜入長安外城，帝奔射雁樓，染焚燒龍尾及諸軍營，殺掠千餘人，旦退屯逍遙園。

translations.literal: Ran entered Chang'an's outer wall by night; the emperor fled to the Wild-Geese Shooting Tower; Ran burned the Dragon Tail and various army camps, killed and plundered over a thousand people; at dawn he withdrew and encamped at Free Roaming Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran stole into Chang'an's outer walls by night; Emperor Min fled to the Goose-Shooting tower while Zhao burned the Dragon Tail bridge and army camps, slaughtered more than a thousand, then pulled back to camp at the Pleasure Garden at dawn.

sentences.zh: 麹允率眾襲曜，連戰敗之。

translations.literal: Qu Yun led troops to raid Yao and defeated him in successive battles.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun struck Liu Yao again and again and drove him from the field.

sentences.zh: 曜入粟邑，遂歸平陽。

translations.literal: Yao entered Suyi, then returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao withdrew to Suyi and then retreated to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 時流星起於牽牛，入紫微，龍形委蛇，其光照地，落於平陽北十里。

translations.literal: At that time a shooting star rose from Ox, entered Purple Forbidden enclosure, dragon-shaped writhing; its light illuminated the ground and fell ten li north of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: A meteor streaked from the Ox asterism into the Purple Forbidden enclosure, twisting like a dragon; its glare lit the earth as it fell ten li north of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 視之，則有肉長三十步，廣二十七步，臭聞於平陽，肉旁常有哭聲，晝夜不止。

translations.literal: Looking at it, there was flesh thirty paces long and twenty-seven wide; the stench reached Pingyang; beside the flesh there was often weeping sound, day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: There lay a slab of flesh thirty paces long and twenty-seven wide; the stench rolled through Pingyang, and unseen voices wept beside it day and night.

sentences.zh: 聰甚惡之，延公卿已下問曰：「朕之不德，致有斯異，其各極言，勿有所諱。

translations.literal: Cong greatly abominated it; he summoned dukes and ministers downward and asked: "Our lack of virtue has brought about this prodigy; each of you speak to the utmost—do not hold back."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong loathed the omen and summoned his ministers: "My want of virtue has caused this portent—speak freely and hide nothing."

sentences.zh: 」陳元達及博士張師等進對曰：「星變之異，其禍行及，臣恐後庭有三后之事，亡國喪家，靡不由此，願陛下慎之。

translations.literal: " Chen Yuanda and erudite Zhang Shi and others stepped forward and replied: "In prodigies of stellar change, their calamity follows in train; your servant fears that in the rear palace there will be affairs of three empresses—loss of state and destruction of family never fail to stem from this—may Your Majesty be careful."
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Yuanda and academician Zhang Shi answered, "When stars misalign, disaster follows. We fear rival empresses will tear the harem apart—dynasties fall from such strife—please tread carefully, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「此陰陽之理，何關人事！

translations.literal: " Cong said: "This is the pattern of yin and yang—what has it to do with human affairs!"
translations.idiomatic: " Liu Cong retorted, "That is only yin and yang shifting—what has it to do with men!"

sentences.zh: 」既而劉氏產一蛇一猛獸，各害人而走，尋之不得，頃之，見在隕肉之旁。

translations.literal: " Soon Lady Liu gave birth to one snake and one fierce beast; each harmed people and fled; searching for them they could not be found; shortly they appeared beside the fallen flesh.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Empress Liu bore a serpent and a savage beast; both injured attendants and vanished until they reappeared beside the meteoric flesh.

sentences.zh: 俄而劉氏死，乃失此肉，哭聲亦止。

translations.literal: Soon Lady Liu died; then this flesh disappeared; the weeping sounds also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liu died soon afterward; the monstrous flesh vanished and the keening ceased.

sentences.zh: 自是後宮亂寵，進禦無序矣。

translations.literal: From this time the rear palace was chaotic in favor; attendance at the imperial bed lacked order.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the harem descended into jealous chaos and the emperor's nights knew no proper order.

sentences.zh: 聰以劉易為太尉。

translations.literal: Cong appointed Liu Yi as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong named Liu Yi grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 初置相國，官上公，有殊勳德者死乃贈之。

translations.literal: For the first time he established the office of chancellor of state, rank supreme duke; those with outstanding merit and virtue received it posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: He created the office of chancellor of state, supreme among dukes, awarded posthumously only to men of extraordinary merit.

sentences.zh: 於是大定百官，置太師、丞相，自大司馬以上七公，位皆上公，綠綟綬，遠遊冠。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly fixed the hundred offices, establishing Grand Preceptor, chancellor; from Grand Marshal upward seven dukes—their rank all supreme duke, green-black ribbons, far-roaming caps.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the bureaucracy, installing grand preceptor and chancellor among seven superior dukes from grand marshal upward—each ranked as supreme duke with green-black ribbons and far-roaming caps.

sentences.zh: 置輔漢，都護，中軍，上軍，輔軍，鎮、衛京，前、後、左、右、上、下軍，輔國，冠軍，龍驤，武牙大將軍，營各配兵二千，皆以諸子為之。

translations.literal: He established Aid-Han, supreme protector, central army, upper army, auxiliary army, garrison and capital guard, front, rear, left, right, upper, lower armies, aid-state, champion, dragon-general, military inspector grand generals—each camp assigned two thousand troops, all filled by various sons.
translations.idiomatic: He created grand commands—Aid Han, protector-in-chief, central, upper, and auxiliary armies, capital garrison and guard, six directional armies, plus aid-state, champion, dragon-general, and military-inspector posts—two thousand soldiers each, every command given to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 置左右司隸，各領戶二十餘萬，萬戶置一內史，凡內史四十三。

translations.literal: He established left and right metropolitan governors, each commanding over two hundred thousand households; for every ten thousand households one interior clerk was set—forty-three interior clerks in all.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right metropolitan intendants each oversaw more than two hundred thousand households with one clerk per ten thousand—forty-three clerks altogether.

sentences.zh: 單于左右輔，各主六夷十萬落，萬落置一都尉。

translations.literal: Chanyu left and right assistants each commanded one hundred thousand barbarian settlements of six kinds; for every ten thousand settlements one commandant was set.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right assistants to the chanyu governed one hundred thousand tribal settlements each, one commandant per ten thousand settlements.

sentences.zh: 省吏部，置左右選曹尚書。

translations.literal: He abolished the Ministry of Personnel and established left and right Bureau of Selection directors.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Ministry of Personnel and installed left and right directors for selection.

sentences.zh: 自司隸以下六官，皆位次僕射。

translations.literal: From metropolitan governor downward six offices—all ranked next after vice directors.
translations.idiomatic: The six offices below the metropolitan intendants ranked immediately after the vice directors.

sentences.zh: 置御史大夫及州牧，位皆亞公。

translations.literal: He established grandee secretary and shepherds of provinces—all ranks next below duke.
translations.idiomatic: He added imperial counselors and provincial governors, each ranking just below duke.

sentences.zh: 以其子粲為丞相、領大將軍、錄尚書事，進封晉王，食五都。

translations.literal: He appointed his son Can chancellor, concurrent grand general, recorder of Masters of Writing affairs, advanced his enfeoffment to Prince of Jin, feeding from five commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He named Liu Can chancellor and concurrent grand general with authority over the Masters of Writing, elevated him to prince of Jin with revenue from five metropolitan districts.

sentences.zh: 劉延年錄尚書六條事，劉景為太師，王育為太傅，任顗為太保，馬景為大司徒，朱紀為大司空，劉曜為大司馬。

translations.literal: Liu Yannian recorder of Masters of Writing six articles of business; Liu Jing as Grand Preceptor; Wang Yu as Grand Tutor; Ren Yi as Grand Guardian; Ma Jing as Grand Minister over the Masses; Zhu Ji as Minister of Works; Liu Yao as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yannian oversaw the six portfolios of the Masters of Writing; Liu Jing became grand preceptor; Wang Yu grand tutor; Ren Yi grand guardian; Ma Jing minister over the masses; Zhu Ji minister of works; Liu Yao grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 曜復次渭汭，趙染次新豐。

translations.literal: Yao again encamped at the Wei bend; Zhao Ran encamped at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao camped again at the bend of the Wei while Zhao Ran positioned himself at Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 索綝自長安東討染，染狃於累捷，有輕綝之色。

translations.literal: Suo Lin from Chang'an attacked Ran eastward; Ran was accustomed to successive victories and showed a look of contempt for Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Lin marched east from Chang'an against Zhao Ran, who had grown cocky after repeated victories and sneered at Suo Lin.

sentences.zh: 長史魯徽曰：「今司馬鄴君臣自以逼僭王畿，雄劣不同，必致死距我，將軍宜整陣案兵以擊之，弗可輕也。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Lu Hui said: "Now Sima Ye's lord and ministers themselves consider they press on the royal capital region—strong and weak are not the same—they will surely fight to the death to oppose us; the general ought to array formations and hold troops to strike them—it cannot be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Lu Hui warned, "Emperor Min and his ministers feel the capital at their backs—strong and weak alike will fight to the death. Marshal your lines and strike carefully—do not underestimate them."

sentences.zh: 困獸猶鬥，況于國乎！

translations.literal: A cornered beast still fights—how much more a state!
translations.idiomatic: Even a trapped beast will fight—what of an embattled kingdom!

sentences.zh: 」染曰：「以司馬模之強，吾取之如拉朽。

translations.literal: " Ran said: "Given Sima Mo's strength, I took him as splitting rotten wood."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran sneered, "When I crushed Prince Sima Mo it was like snapping rotten wood.

sentences.zh: 索綝小豎，豈能汙吾馬蹄刀刃邪！

translations.literal: Suo Lin is a petty boy—how can he defile my horse hooves and blade edges!
translations.idiomatic: How could a nobody like Suo Lin bloody my blade or my stirrup!

sentences.zh: 要擒之而後食。

translations.literal: I intend to capture him and then eat.
translations.idiomatic: I will bag him before I sit down to eat."

sentences.zh: 」晨率精騎數百，馳出逆之，戰於城西，敗績而歸，悔曰：「吾不用魯徽之言，以至於此，何面見之！

translations.literal: " At dawn he led several hundred picked horse, galloped out to oppose him, fought west of the city, returned routed, and regretted: "I did not use Lu Hui's words—to reach this point—what face have I to see him!"
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn he charged west of the city with a few hundred riders and fled in defeat. "I ignored Lu Hui," he groaned, "and now I cannot face him!"

sentences.zh: 」於是斬徽。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he executed Hui.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he executed Lu Hui.

sentences.zh: 徽臨刑謂染曰：「將軍愎諫違謀，戇而取敗，而復忌前害勝，誅戮忠良，以逞愚忿，亦何顏面瞬息世間哉！

translations.literal: Hui facing execution said to Ran: "The general stubbornly rejected counsel and violated strategy, foolishly took defeat, yet again envied the advanced and harmed the victorious, executed and slaughtered the loyal and good to vent foolish rage—what face have you to linger a moment in this world!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui told Zhao Ran at the block, "You spurned wise counsel, rushed to defeat, murdered loyal men to soothe your pride—how dare you walk among honest folk another hour!"

sentences.zh: 袁紹為之于前，將軍踵之于後，覆亡敗喪，亦當相尋，所恨不得一見大司馬而死。

translations.literal: Yuan Shao did it before him; the general treads after—overthrow and defeat ought likewise to follow in succession; what your servant regrets is not being able once to see the Grand Marshal before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shao walked this road before you—you follow his footsteps, and ruin will follow you. My only regret is dying before I could warn Grand Marshal Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 死者無知則已；

translations.literal: If the dead have no awareness, then enough;
translations.idiomatic: If the dead feel nothing, then silence;

sentences.zh: 若其有知，下見田豐為徒，要當訴將軍于黃泉，使將軍不得服床枕而死。

translations.literal: if they have awareness, below he will see Tian Feng as companion—surely he will indict the general in the Yellow Springs and make the general unable to die on bed and pillow.
translations.idiomatic: but if consciousness survives death, I shall walk with Tian Feng in the underworld and indict you in the Yellow Springs until you die far from your couch.

sentences.zh: 」叱刑者曰：「令吾面東向。

translations.literal: " He shouted to the executioners: "Make my face turn eastward."
translations.idiomatic: " He shouted to the headsman, "Turn me to face east—toward the Jin court."

sentences.zh: 」大司馬曜聞之曰：「蹄涔不容尺鯉，染之謂也。」

translations.literal: " Grand Marshal Yao hearing it said: "A hoof-print puddle cannot hold a carp—this speaks of Ran."
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Marshal Liu Yao remarked, "They say a hoof-print pool cannot hide a carp—that fits Zhao Ran to the inch."

sentences.zh: 曜還師攻郭默於懷城，收其米粟八十萬斛，列三屯以守之。

translations.literal: Yao returned his army to attack Guo Mo at Huai city, seized his grain eight hundred thousand hu, and arrayed three camps to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao doubled back to strike Guo Mo at Huai, confiscated eight hundred thousand hu of grain, and planted three garrisons to hold it.

sentences.zh: 聰遣使謂曜曰：「今長安假息，劉琨遊魂，此國家所尤宜先除也。

translations.literal: Cong sent envoys to say to Yao: "Now Chang'an draws false breath; Liu Kun is a roaming soul—this is what the state most ought first to eliminate."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong sent Liu Yao word: "Chang'an still flickers with life and Liu Kun wanders like a ghost—both demand our first strike."

sentences.zh: 郭默小丑，何足以勞公神略，可留征虜將軍貝丘王翼光守之，公其還也。

translations.literal: Guo Mo is a petty rascal; how could he suffice to weary your divine strategy? You may leave General Who Strikes Down the Barbarians Wang Yiguang, Prince of Beiqu, to hold him; as for you, sir, you ought to return.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo is a negligible foe—hardly worth straining your stratagem. Leave General Who Crushes the Barbarians Wang Yiguang of Beiqu to pin him in place and withdraw yourself.

sentences.zh: 」於是曜歸薄阪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Yao returned to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: When the message was delivered Liu Yao marched back to Puban.

sentences.zh: 俄而徵曜輔政。

translations.literal: Before long [the court] summoned Yao to aid in governing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liu Cong recalled Liu Yao to steer state affairs.

sentences.zh: 趙染寇北地，夢魯徽大怒，引弓射之，染驚悸而寤。

translations.literal: Zhao Ran raided Beidi; he dreamed that Lu Hui was greatly enraged, drew his bow, and shot him; Zhao Ran woke alarmed and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding Beidi, Zhao Ran dreamed Lu Hui raging, bent a bow, and loosed a shaft at him—he jolted awake petrified.

sentences.zh: 旦將攻城，中弩而死。

translations.literal: When dawn came he was about to assault the city and was struck by a crossbow bolt and died.
translations.idiomatic: At sunrise, on the point of scaling the walls, he caught a quarrel and fell dead.

sentences.zh: 聰以粲為相國，總百揆，省丞相以並相國。

translations.literal: Liu Cong appointed Liu Can Chancellor of State, superintended the hundred administrations, abolished the office of Chancellor, and consolidated its duties with the Chancellorship of State.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong installed Liu Can as chancellor of state atop every ministry, then abolished the old chancellor title so that authority pooled in that office alone.

sentences.zh: 平陽地震，烈風拔樹髮屋。

translations.literal: Pingyang shook in an earthquake; fierce winds uprooted trees and tore off roofs.
translations.idiomatic: Quakes rocked Pingyang while gales uprooted timber and stripped roofs away.

sentences.zh: 光義人羊充妻產子二頭，其兄竊而食之，三日而死。

translations.literal: One Yang Chong's wife among the people of Guangyi gave birth to a two-headed infant; her elder brother stole it and ate it and died after three days.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangyi commoner Yang Chong's wife bore a dicephalic child; her elder brother stole it, consumed it, and dropped dead three days later.

sentences.zh: 聰以其太廟新成，大赦境內，改年建元。

translations.literal: Liu Cong, because his dynastic Grand Temple was newly finished, declared a great amnesty within the borders and changed the reign period to Founding Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrating the completion of his ancestral shrine, Liu Cong issued an empire-wide amnesty and adopted the Jiànyuan era.

sentences.zh: 雨血於其東宮延明殿，徹瓦在地者深五寸。

translations.literal: Blood rained upon his Eastern Palace Yanming Hall; where tiles had fallen to earth the depth reached five cun.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson showers drenched Yanming Hall in the heir's precinct, pooling five cun deep over shattered tiles.

sentences.zh: 劉乂惡之，以訪其太師盧志、太傅崔瑋、太保許遐。

translations.literal: Liu Yi abhorred these things and consulted his grand preceptor Lu Zhi, grand tutor Cui Wei, and grand guardian Xu Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi read the prodigies with dread and took counsel from Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia.

sentences.zh: 志等曰：「主上往以殿下為太弟者，蓋以安眾望也，志在晉王久矣，王公已下莫不希旨歸之。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi and the others said: "The sovereign once named Your Highness heir apparent solely to placate widespread expectation; his purpose has leaned toward the Prince of Jin for ages, and none from royal dukes downward fails to read that intent and cling to him.
translations.idiomatic: "The throne-maker made you heir only to soothe the court," they said; "his eye has rested on Liu Can for years, and every grandee follows that drift."

sentences.zh: 相國之位，自魏武已來，非復人臣之官，主上本發明詔，置之為贈官，今忽以晉王居之，羽儀威尊逾于東宮，萬機之事無不由之，置太宰、大將軍及諸王之營以為羽翼，此事勢去矣，殿下不得立明也。

translations.literal: Since the era of Wei Wu the Chancellorship of State has ceased to be a servant's commission; our lord issued an explicit rule treating it as a posthumously bestowed dignity. Suddenly the Prince of Jin fills it—the panoply of guards and ceremonial majesty outstrip the Eastern Palace, and none of the myriad policy threads bypass him.
