He has stationed the grand steward, the grand marshal, and the princes' military camps as wings. With power arrayed thus, momentum has slipped away—you cannot openly expect to ascend."
translations.idiomatic: "Since Cao Cao the super-chancellorship overshadows mere ministers; your father barred living men from that title save as posthumous glory—yet Liu Can now occupies it with retinues grander than the crown prince's while every edict crosses his desk, flanked by steward, marshal, and royal hosts. Succession no longer visibly belongs to you."

sentences.zh: 然非止不得立而已，不測之危厄在於旦夕，宜早為之所。

translations.literal: Yet even failure to ascend is hardly the worst; immeasurable calamity threatens by every dawn—you must prepare early.
translations.idiomatic: "Worse than losing the succession is imminent ruin—strike before catastrophe finds you."

sentences.zh: 四衛精兵不減五千，余營諸王皆年齒尚幼，可奪而取之。

translations.literal: The four guards' elite still number no fewer than five thousand; the other princes' encampments are led by youths—you can wrench them away.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guard corps fields five thousand veterans, and child princes hold the outlying camps—both are there for the seizing.

sentences.zh: 相國輕佻，正可煩一刺客耳。

translations.literal: The Chancellor of State is rash; vexing yourself with armies is needless—a single dagger will do.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can is reckless—hire one blade and remove him.

sentences.zh: 大將軍無日不出，其營可襲而得也。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal exposes himself daily; ravage his lines and seize them outright.
translations.idiomatic: The grand marshal rides out without fail—ambush his headquarters and overpower it.

sentences.zh: 殿下但當有意，二萬精兵立便可得，鼓行向雲龍門，宿衛之士孰不倒戈奉迎，大司馬不慮為異也。

translations.literal: Your Highness need only form the intent—twenty thousand picked soldiers may be gathered at once; beat drums toward the Yunlong Gate and which of the night-watch troops will not cast spears aside to hail you? The Grand Marshal should not presume to dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Authorize the coup and twenty thousand veterans can march straight to Yunlong Gate, where night sentinels will gladly switch sides; the grand marshal will not obstruct you.

sentences.zh: 」乂弗從，乃止。

translations.literal: " Liu Yi would not heed them, and they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi refused, and the plot collapsed.

sentences.zh: 聰如中護軍靳准第，納其二女為左右貴嬪，大曰月光，小曰月華，皆國色也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong went to Chief Commandant of the Guards Jin Zhun's residence, took his two daughters as left and right Honored Concubines, the elder titled Moon Gleam, the younger Moon Bloom; both were beauties of national renown.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong visited Jin Zhun's mansion and inducted his daughters as left and right “noble beauties,” the elder Lady Moon Gleam and the younger Lady Moon Bloom, women famed through the realm.

sentences.zh: 數月，立月光為皇后。

translations.literal: Several months later he established Moon Gleam as Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Lady Moon Gleam was elevated to empress.

sentences.zh: 東宮舍人荀裕告盧志等勸乂謀反，乂不從之狀。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace steward Xun Yu reported the circumstance of Lu Zhi and others exhorting Liu Yi to rebel and Liu Yi refusing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yu, an aide in the heir's household, denounced Lu Zhi's circle for urging revolt on Liu Yi—counsel Yi had rejected.

sentences.zh: 聰於是收志、瑋、遐於詔獄，假以他事殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Cong arrested Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia in a prison opened by edict and, under other pretexts, executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong jailed Lu Zhi, Cui Wei, and Xu Xia on manufactured charges and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 使冠威卜抽監守東宮，禁乂朝賀。

translations.literal: He ordered Guanwei Bu Chou to supervise and guard the Eastern Palace and forbade Liu Yi from attending court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Bu Chou, colonel of the crown guards, on the heir's mansion and barred Liu Yi from court felicitations.

sentences.zh: 乂憂懼不知所為，乃上表自陳，乞為黔首，並免諸子之封，褒美晉王粲宜登儲副，抽又抑而弗通。

translations.literal: Yi, anxious and afraid, not knowing what to do, submitted a memorial stating himself, begging to become a black-haired commoner, together canceling enfeoffments for all his sons, extolling the Prince of Jin Can as fit to rise to the secondary heir—Draw moreover suppressed it and did not transmit it.
translations.idiomatic: Panicking, Liu Yi offered to become a commoner, strip his sons of titles, and praise Liu Can as successor—Bu Draw buried the petition.

sentences.zh: 其青州刺史曹嶷攻汶陽關、公丘，陷之，害齊郡太守徐浮，執建威劉宣，齊魯之間郡縣壘壁降者四十餘所。

translations.literal: His governor of Qingzhou Cao Yi attacked Wenyang Pass and Gongqiu, overran them, killed Grand Administrator of Qi Commandery Xu Fu, captured General Who Establishes Might Liu Xuan, and between Qi and Lu more than forty county seats and fortresses surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi of Qingzhou stormed Wenyang barrier and Gongqiu, slew Qi prefect Xu Fu, took Liu Xuan captive, and brought over forty citadels between Qi and Lu to heel.

sentences.zh: 嶷遂略地，西下祝阿、平陰，眾十餘萬，臨河置戍，而歸於臨淄。

translations.literal: Cao Yi thereupon extended his territory, marched west to capture Zhu'a and Pingyin, massed more than a hundred thousand men, posted river garrisons, and returned to Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: He swept west through Zhu'a and Pingyin, raised above a hundred thousand warriors, seeded pickets along the Yellow River, and pulled back toward Linzi.

sentences.zh: 嶷於是遂雄據全齊之志。

translations.literal: Cao Yi thereupon conceived the ambition of heroically dominating the whole of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: From there Cao Yi intended to make himself master of all Qi.

sentences.zh: 石勒以嶷之懷二也，請討之。

translations.literal: Shi Le, because Cao Yi nursed duplicity, requested permission to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, scenting disloyalty in Cao Yi, asked to crush him.

sentences.zh: 聰又憚勒之並齊，乃寢而弗許。

translations.literal: Liu Cong again feared Shi Le's annexation of Qi, and therefore tabled the matter and did not grant approval.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, afraid Shi Le would swallow Shandong, shelved the request.

sentences.zh: 劉曜濟自盟津，將攻河南，將軍魏該奔於一泉塢。

translations.literal: Liu Yao crossed at Meng Ford intending to attack Henan; General Wei Gai fled to Yiquan stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao forded Mengjin to overrun Henan while commander Wei Gai escaped to the Yiquan redoubt.

sentences.zh: 曜進攻李矩于滎陽，矩遣將軍李平師于成皋，曜覆而滅之。

translations.literal: Yao advanced to attack Li Ju at Yingyang; Ju sent General Li Ping, who encamped at Chenggao; Yao enveloped and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Besieging Li Ju at Yingyang, Liu Yao crushed Li Ping's Chenggao camp in a envelopment.

sentences.zh: 矩恐，送質請降。

translations.literal: Ju, frightened, sent hostages begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Terror-struck, Li Ju forwarded hostages to sue for terms.

sentences.zh: 時聰以其皇后靳氏為上皇后，立貴妃劉氏為左皇后，右貴嬪靳氏為右皇后。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Cong took his Empress Lady Jin as Senior Empress, established Honored Concubine Lady Liu as Left Empress, and Right Honored Concubine Lady Jin as Right Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong simultaneously enthroned Empress Jin as “chief empress,” a Lady Liu as left empress, and a second Lady Jin as right empress.

sentences.zh: 左司隸陳元達以三后之立也，極諫，聰不納，乃以元達為右光祿大夫，外示優賢，內實奪其權也。

translations.literal: Left Metropolitan Commandant Chen Yuanda, over the establishment of three empresses, remonstrated to the utmost; Liu Cong did not accept it, and therefore made Yuanda Right Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor, outwardly displaying favor to worthies while inwardly stripping his authority.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda protested the triple queens in vain; Liu Cong “promoted” him to Right Grand Master of Brilliant Splendor—a hollow honour that severed his power.

sentences.zh: 於是太尉范隆、大司馬劉丹、大司空呼延晏、尚書令王鑒等皆抗表遜位，以讓元達。

translations.literal: Thereupon Defender-in-chief Fan Long, Grand Marshal Liu Dan, Minister of Works Huyan Yan, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian, and others all submitted memorials declining office to yield to Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long, Liu Dan, Huyan Yan, Wang Jian, and others resigned in concert to force Chen Yuanda's reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 聰乃以元達為御史大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Liu Cong thereupon appointed Yuanda Censor-in-chief with peer standing of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong relented, naming Chen Yuanda chief censor with Three-Duke protocol.

sentences.zh: 劉曜寇長安，頻為王師所敗。

translations.literal: Liu Yao raided Chang'an and was repeatedly defeated by the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao struck at Chang'an but Jin troops drove him back again and again.

sentences.zh: 曜曰：「彼猶強盛，弗可圖矣。

translations.literal: Yao said: "They remain strong; they cannot be schemed against.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao judged, “The enemy is still too mighty to overthrow.”

sentences.zh: 」引師而歸。

translations.literal: " He led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: He broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 聰宮中鬼夜哭，三日而聲向右司隸寺，乃止。

translations.literal: In Liu Cong's palace ghosts wept by night; after three days the sound shifted to the right metropolitan commandant's office, then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Spectral wailing haunted Liu Cong's harem for three nights before migrating to the right metropolitan jail and dying away.

sentences.zh: 其上皇后靳氏有淫穢之行，陳元達奏之。

translations.literal: His Senior Empress Lady Jin had conduct of lewdness; Chen Yuanda memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief empress Jin was caught in debauchery; Chen Yuanda impeached her.

sentences.zh: 聰廢靳，靳慚恚自殺。

translations.literal: Liu Cong deposed Jin; Jin, ashamed and enraged, committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong cast her aside; distraught with shame, she took her life.

sentences.zh: 靳有殊寵，聰迫于元達之勢，故廢之。

translations.literal: Jin had enjoyed extraordinary favour; Liu Cong, pressured by Yuanda's influence, therefore deposed her.
translations.idiomatic: She had been Liu Cong's favourite, yet he discarded her beneath Chen Yuanda's moral sway.

sentences.zh: 既而追念其姿色，深仇元達。

translations.literal: Afterwards he recalled her beauty and nursed bitter hatred toward Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he brooded on her charms and harboured deep resentment against Chen Yuanda.

sentences.zh: 劉曜進師上黨，將攻陽曲，聰遣使謂曜曰：「長安擅命，國家之深恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao advanced troops to Shangdang intending to attack Yangqu; Liu Cong dispatched messengers telling Yao: "Chang'an's arrogant assumption of mandate is our dynasty's profound shame.
translations.idiomatic: Marching from Shangdang on Yangqu, Liu Yao received Liu Cong's order: “Jin's grip on Chang'an shames us most.”

sentences.zh: 公宜以長安為先，陽曲一委驃騎。

translations.literal: You ought to place Chang'an first; leave Yangqu entirely to the Cavalry-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Strike Chang'an first and leave Yangqu wholly to your cavalry marshal.

sentences.zh: 天時人事，其應至矣，公其亟還。

translations.literal: Heaven's seasons and human affairs—their convergence has arrived; you, sir, should hurry back.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and men both align—return without delay.

sentences.zh: 」曜回滅郭邁，朝於聰，遂如蒲阪。

translations.literal: " Yao wheeled about, extinguished Guo Mai, had audience with Liu Cong, and proceeded to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao swung his host, wiped out Guo Mai, paid homage at Pingyang, and moved on to Puban.

sentences.zh: 平陽地震，雨血於東宮，廣袤頃餘。

translations.literal: Pingyang shook in an earthquake; blood rained on the Eastern Palace covering more than a qing.
translations.idiomatic: Another temblor hit Pingyang while gore showered the heir's compound across over a qing of ground.

sentences.zh: 劉曜又進軍，屯於粟邑。

translations.literal: Liu Yao again advanced the army and encamped at Suiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao pushed forward again and camped at Suiyi.

sentences.zh: 麹允饑甚，去黃白而軍于靈武。

translations.literal: Qu Yun was exceedingly famished; he abandoned Huangbai and encamped at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun, starving, quit the Huangbai stronghold for Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 曜進攻上郡，太守張禹與馮翊太守梁肅奔於允吾。

translations.literal: Yao attacked Shang Commandery; Grand Administrator Zhang Yu with Grand Administrator of Fengyi Liang Su fled to Yunwu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao stormed Shang—prefect Zhang Yu fled with Fengyi's Liang Su toward Yunwu.

sentences.zh: 於是關右翕然，所在應曜。

translations.literal: Thereupon west of the passes all murmured assent; everywhere they answered Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest of Tong Pass the country murmured and rose to Liu Yao's call.

sentences.zh: 曜進據黃阜。

translations.literal: Yao advanced and occupied Huangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the Huangfu heights.

sentences.zh: 聰武庫陷入地一丈五尺。

translations.literal: Liu Cong's armoury sank into earth one zhang five chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong's arsenal yard subsided fifteen chi into the soil.

sentences.zh: 時聰中常侍王沈、宣懷、俞容，中宮僕射郭猗，中黃門陵修等皆寵倖用事。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Cong's palace attendants Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, and Yu Rong, Central Palace Supervisor Guo Yi, and Yellow Gate Ling Xiu and others were all favoured favourites wielding affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch favourites—Wang Shen, Xuan Huai, Yu Rong, Guo Yi the inner-palace steward, Ling Xiu of the Yellow Gate, and their ilk—ran the regime.

sentences.zh: 聰游宴後宮，或百日不出，群臣皆因沈等言事，多不呈聰，率以其意愛憎而決之，故或有勳舊功臣而弗見敘錄，奸佞小人數日而便至二千石者。

translations.literal: Liu Cong roved and banqueted in the rear palaces; sometimes a hundred days without emerging; all officials relayed business through Shen and company, much of which never reached Liu Cong; broadly they resolved matters by their personal loves and hates—hence sometimes meritorious old ministers went unrecorded while sycophantic petty men reached two-thousand-shi rank within days.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong caroused behind vermilion walls for months on end while ministers routed paperwork through Wang Shen's clique—seldom reaching the throne—so favours alone decided posts, skipping venerable heroes while toadies jumped to fat salaries overnight.

sentences.zh: 軍旅無歲不興，而將士無錢帛之賞，後宮之家賜齎及於僮僕，動至數千萬。

translations.literal: Armies marched every year yet commanders received no grants of coin or silk; households of the rear palaces were gifted to the point of servants and pages, routinely reaching tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns never ceased, yet troops went unpaid; imperial concubines showered slaves with gifts running into tens of millions of cash.

sentences.zh: 沈等車服宅宇皆逾于諸王，子弟、中表布衣為內史令長者三十餘人，皆奢僭貪殘，賊害良善。

translations.literal: Shen and company—carriages, robes, dwellings, all exceeded those of the princes; more than thirty of their sons and cousins-by-marriage became commoners appointed commandery administrators or magistrates, all extravagant, overweening, greedy, cruel, looting and killing the good.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen's cabal flaunted carriages and mansions finer than princes', placing thirty-plus kinsmen as local magistrates—luxury-mad plunderers one and all.

sentences.zh: 靳准合宗內外諂以事之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun assembled his whole clan inside and outside to flatter and serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun rallied his entire kin to curry favour with them.

sentences.zh: 郭猗有憾于劉乂，謂劉粲曰：「太弟于主上之世猶懷不逞之志，此則殿下父子之深仇，四海蒼生之重怨也。

translations.literal: Guo Yi nursed a grudge toward Liu Yi and said to Liu Can: "During the Sovereign's lifetime the heir-apparent brother still harbors unbridled ambitions—this is deep enmity between Your Highness and your father as well as the heavy resentment of all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi, nursing spite against Liu Yi, whispered to Liu Can, “While your father yet rules, your uncle the heir cherishes ambitions that make you mortal enemies and turn the realm against him.”

sentences.zh: 而主上過垂寬仁，猶不替二尊之位，一旦有風塵之變，臣竊為殿下寒心。

translations.literal: Yet the Sovereign has been excessively lenient and still does not remove the two exalted seats; once storm winds of change arise, your servant secretly shivers for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: “Yet the emperor indulges him and leaves both thrones untouched—when crisis breaks you will suffer first.”

sentences.zh: 且殿下高祖之世孫，主上之嫡統，凡在含齒，孰不系仰。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Highness is the great-grandson of Gaozu and the Sovereign's legitimate line—whoever bears teeth fails to hang his hopes on you.
translations.idiomatic: “You alone are Gaozu's great-grandson and the true imperial line—every citizen looks to you.”

sentences.zh: 萬機事大，何可與人！

translations.literal: The myriad handles are too great—how may they be shared with another!
translations.idiomatic: “The purple business is not for sharing.”

sentences.zh: 臣昨聞太弟與大將軍相見，極有言矣，若事成，許以主上為在太上皇，大將軍為皇太子。

translations.literal: Yesterday I heard the heir-apparent brother and the Grand Marshal met and held deep talks; should the enterprise succeed they pledged to reset the Sovereign as Retired August Throne-holder and install the Grand Marshal as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: “Yesterday your uncle huddled with the grand marshal; if they win they plan to pension the Son of Heaven as 'supreme father' and crown the marshal heir.”

sentences.zh: 乂又許衛軍為大單于，二王已許之矣。

translations.literal: Liu Yi moreover promised the Guards-general the Great Chanyu; the two royal lords have already assented.
translations.idiomatic: “They even promised the guard-general the title of grand chanyu—both princes agreed.”

sentences.zh: 二王居不疑之地，並握重兵，以此舉事，事何不成！

translations.literal: The two royal lords sit in unquestioned stations and jointly grip heavy armies—undertaking affairs on this footing, how can the matter fail!
translations.idiomatic: “Each holds unquestioned rank and veteran legions—their plot cannot miss.”

sentences.zh: 臣謂二王茲舉，禽獸之不若也。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that for this action of the two royal lords not even beasts would be their match.
translations.idiomatic: “Their scheme is viler than beasts.”

sentences.zh: 背父親人，人豈親之！

translations.literal: Those who turn their backs on fathers and kin—how should others treat them as kin!
translations.idiomatic: “Men who sell out father and brother win no loyalty.”

sentences.zh: 今又苟貪其一切之力耳，事成之後，主上豈有全理！

translations.literal: Now they moreover greedily grasp at momentary force; once the deed is done, how should the Sovereign remain whole in principle!
translations.idiomatic: “They only covet raw power; once enthroned they will never spare your father.”

sentences.zh: 殿下兄弟故在忘言，東宮、相國、單于在武陵兄弟，何肯與人！

translations.literal: Your Highness and your brothers remain in relations where words are forgotten; the Eastern Palace, Chancellor of State, and Chanyu are Wuling-style brothers—how would they hand [power] to another!
translations.idiomatic: “You still trust fraternal bonds, but heir, chancellor, and chanyu are a Wuling clique—they will never yield the realm.”

sentences.zh: 許以三月上巳因宴作難，事淹變生，宜早為之所。

translations.literal: They pledged on the third month's upper-si festival to raise trouble at a banquet; delay lets schemes shift—you must act early.
translations.idiomatic: “They fixed the spring Shangsi banquet for the coup—hesitation invites disaster.”

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：'蔓草猶不可除，況君之寵弟乎！

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: 'Even rampant weeds cannot be eradicated—how much less a sovereign's cherished younger brother!'
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo warns: 'Runaway grass defies rooting out—let alone a ruler's pet brother.'

sentences.zh: '臣屢啟主上，主上性敦友于，謂臣言不實。

translations.literal: ' Your servant has repeatedly opened his heart to the Sovereign; the Sovereign's nature esteems fraternal duty and deems your servant's words untrue.
translations.idiomatic: “I have warned the throne, but his nature clings to brotherly piety and dismisses me.”

sentences.zh: 刑臣刀鋸之余，而蒙主上、殿下成造之恩，故不慮逆鱗之誅，每所聞必言，冀垂採納。

translations.literal: As the leavings of knife and saw, I yet received the nurturing grace of Sovereign and Your Highness; therefore I do not fear execution for touching the inverse scales—whatever I hear I must speak, hoping you will deign to accept.
translations.idiomatic: “A mutilated retainer whom you both favoured, I still risk regicide talk so you might listen.”

sentences.zh: 臣當入言之。

translations.literal: Your servant will enter and speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: “I shall raise it with the emperor again.”

sentences.zh: 願殿下不泄，密表其狀也。

translations.literal: May Your Highness not leak word; secretly memorialize the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: “Say nothing outwardly—submit a sealed brief instead.”

sentences.zh: 若不信臣言，可呼大將軍從事中郎王皮、衛軍司馬劉惇，假之恩顧，通其歸善之路以問之，必可知也。

translations.literal: If you do not trust your servant's words, summon the Grand Marshal's registrar Wang Pi and the Guard-general's major Liu Dun, grant them gracious regard, open a path that they may return to loyalty, and question them—you can know for certain.
translations.idiomatic: “If you doubt me, coax Wang Pi and Liu Dun with favours—they will confess.”

sentences.zh: 」粲深然之。

translations.literal: " Liu Can fully assented.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can believed every word.

sentences.zh: 猗密謂皮、惇曰：「二王逆狀，主、相已具知之矣，卿同之乎？

translations.literal: Guo Yi secretly told Pi and Dun: "The treason of the two royal lords—Sovereign and Chancellor already fully know of it; do you concur?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi cornered Wang Pi and Liu Dun: “The Son of Heaven and Liu Can already know your princes’ treason—do you?”

sentences.zh: 」二人驚曰？

translations.literal: " The two men cried out in alarm?!
translations.idiomatic: The pair gasped.

sentences.zh: ：「無之。

translations.literal: : "There is nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: They stammered there was no plot.

sentences.zh: 」猗曰：「此事必無疑，吾憐卿親舊並見族耳。

translations.literal: " Guo Yi said: "In this matter there is no doubt; I pity you that kin and old friends will be exterminated wholesale.
translations.idiomatic: “Deny it and your clans burn,” Guo Yi warned.

sentences.zh: 」於是歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they sobbed and shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: He wept theatrically.

sentences.zh: 皮、惇大懼，叩頭求哀。

translations.literal: Pi and Dun were greatly frightened, kowtowed begging mercy.
translations.idiomatic: They fell prostrate, pleading for their lives.

sentences.zh: 猗曰：「吾為卿作計，卿能用不？

translations.literal: " Guo Yi said: "I will devise a plan for you—can you employ it?
translations.idiomatic: “I can save you—will you obey?”

sentences.zh: 」二人皆曰：「謹奉大人之教。

translations.literal: " The two both said: "We respectfully receive the great man's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: “Command us,” they said.

sentences.zh: 」猗曰：「相國必問卿，卿但云有之。

translations.literal: " Guo Yi said: "The Chancellor of State is sure to question you; you need only answer that it is so.
translations.idiomatic: “When Liu Can asks, admit the plot.”

sentences.zh: 若責卿何不先啟，卿即答云：'臣誠負死罪，然仰惟主上聖性寬慈，殿下篤于骨肉，恐言成詿偽故也。

translations.literal: If he reproaches you for why you did not report first, you immediately answer: 'Your servant indeed deserves death, yet looking up I considered the Sovereign's sacred nature magnanimous and Your Highness's devotion to flesh and bone, fearing speech would become slander—hence [silence].
translations.idiomatic: “If he demands why you stayed silent, say you dreaded false witness against a loving father and son.”

sentences.zh: '」皮、惇許諾。

translations.literal: '" Pi and Dun promised.
translations.idiomatic: They swore to the script.

sentences.zh: 粲俄而召問二人，至不同時，而辭若畫一，粲以為信然。

translations.literal: Liu Can shortly thereafter summoned and questioned the two men; arriving at non-identical moments, their wording matched as though drawn with one template—Liu Can believed it true.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can grilled them separately; their stories matched line for line, so he trusted the fraud.

sentences.zh: 初，靳准從妹為乂孺子，淫于侍人，乂怒殺之，而屢以嘲准。

translations.literal: Initially Jin Zhun's cousin by marriage had become Liu Yi's concubine; she committed lewdness with attendants; Liu Yi in anger killed her and repeatedly used the matter to mock Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Jin Zhun's cousin had entered Liu Yi's harem, dallied with pages, and died at Yi's hand—an episode Jin Zhun never forgave.

sentences.zh: 准深慚恚，說粲曰：「東宮萬機之副，殿下宜自居之，以領相國，使天下知早有所系望也。

translations.literal: Zhun deeply resented it and said to Liu Can: "The Eastern Palace is lieutenant to the myriad handles; Your Highness ought yourself to occupy it and superintend the Chancellor of State, letting the realm know early where hopes are fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun urged Liu Can to seize the Eastern Palace and oversee the chancellorship so the world saw where power lay.

sentences.zh: 」至是，准又說粲曰：「昔孝成距子政之言，使王氏卒成篡逆，可乎？

translations.literal: At this point Zhun again said to Liu Can: "Formerly Emperor Cheng rejected Zizheng's counsel and allowed the Wang clan finally to usurp—was that acceptable?
translations.idiomatic: He added, “Emperor Cheng spurned Liu Xiang and let the Wangs usurp—will you repeat it?”

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「何可之有！

translations.literal: " Liu Can said: "How could it be acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: “Never,” said Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 」准曰：「然，誠如聖旨。

translations.literal: " Zhun said: "Indeed; it is truly as the sagely decree.
translations.idiomatic: “Then hear me,” Jin Zhun pressed.

sentences.zh: 下官亟欲有所言矣，但以德非更生，親非皇宗，恐忠言暫出，霜威已及，故不敢耳。

translations.literal: Your humble official has long wished to speak, but because my virtue is not that of Gengsheng and my kinship is not imperial stock, I feared loyal words would hardly leave my mouth before frost-like wrath arrived—therefore I dared not.
translations.idiomatic: “I would have spoken sooner, but lacking Liu Xiang's virtue and royal blood I feared instant death—until now.”

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「君但言之。

translations.literal: " Liu Can said: "You need only speak.
translations.idiomatic: “Speak freely,” Liu Can said.

sentences.zh: 」准曰：「聞風塵之言，謂大將軍、衛將軍及左右輔皆謀奉太弟，克季春構變，殿下宜為之備。

translations.literal: " Zhun said: "Rumour on the wind says the Grand Marshal, Guard-general, and left and right assistants all plot to enthrone the heir-apparent brother, will complete the mutiny in late spring—Your Highness ought to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun closed: “Word says the marshal, guard-general, and aides mean to crown your uncle this spring—arm yourself.”

sentences.zh: 不然，恐有商臣之禍。

translations.literal: If it is not so, I fear there will be Shangchen’s calamity [of parricide].
translations.idiomatic: If we do otherwise, Your Highness may bring down the doom that seized Crown Prince Shangchen of Chu.

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「為之奈何？

translations.literal: ’ Liu Can said, ‘What is to be done about it?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can asked, “What, then, should we do?”

sentences.zh: 」准曰：「主上愛信于太弟，恐卒聞未必信也。

translations.literal: ’ Jin Zhun said, ‘The Lord above loves and trusts the Grand Heir; I fear if he hears of it suddenly he may not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun answered, “His Majesty dotes on the heir apparent; a sudden accusation may not convince him.”

sentences.zh: 如下官愚意，宜緩東宮之禁固，勿絕太弟賓客，使輕薄之徒得與交遊。

translations.literal: According to this inferior official’s foolish view, one should loosen the Eastern Palace’s strict confinement, not cut off the Grand Heir’s guests, allowing frivolous fellows to mingle with him.
translations.idiomatic: My counsel is this: ease the cordon round the heir’s residence and let his visitors come and go—especially empty-headed hangers-on.

sentences.zh: 太弟既素好待士，必不思防此嫌，輕薄小人不能無逆意以勸太弟之心。

translations.literal: The Grand Heir has always been fond of treating scholars well; he will surely not think to guard against this suspicion; petty frivolous men cannot fail to harbour rebellious ideas to spur the Grand Heir’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loves patronizing gentlemen; he will never suspect such company, and shallow opportunists will surely whisper sedition into his willing ear.

sentences.zh: 小人有始無終，不能如貫高之流也。

translations.literal: Petty men have a beginning and no end; they cannot be like the sort of Guan Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Such rogues never finish what they begin; none of them proves another Guan Gao, mute unto death.

sentences.zh: 然後下官為殿下露表其罪，殿下與太宰拘太弟所與交通者考問之，窮其事原，主上必以無將之罪罪之。

translations.literal: Then this inferior official shall for Your Highness expose his crimes in a memorial; Your Highness and the Grand Governor shall arrest those persons with whom the Grand Heir has associated, interrogate them, and probe the affair to its source—the Lord above is sure to convict him under the statutes on unauthorised revolt against the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Next I draft a memorial denouncing him; Your Highness and the grand governor seize his circle, wring out the conspiracy, and His Majesty must condemn him for treason.

sentences.zh: 不然，今朝望多歸太弟，主上一旦晏駕，恐殿下不得立矣。

translations.literal: If not, now hopes of dawn court mostly go to the Grand Heir; if the Lord above one day mounts the dark carriage [dies], I fear Your Highness will not be established.
translations.idiomatic: If not, morning court already looks to the heir; the day His Majesty dies, Your Highness may never mount the throne.

sentences.zh: 」於是粲命卜抽引兵去東宮。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon Liu Can ordered Bu Chou to lead troops away from the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can then told Bu Chou to withdraw his soldiers from around the heir’s palace.

sentences.zh: 聰自去冬至是，遂不復受朝賀，軍國之事一決於粲，唯發中旨殺生除授，王沈、郭猗等意所欲皆從之。

translations.literal: From last winter unto this Liu Cong no longer accepted New Year congratulations; military and civil affairs were wholly decided by Liu Can; only inner-palace edicts on executions, promotions, dismissals issued forth—and whatsoever Wang Shen, Guo Yi, and others desired was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the winter before, Liu Cong had skipped court receptions; Liu Can ruled every matter of state while palace slips alone carried out killings and appointments—and Wang Shen, Guo Yi, and company always won their whim.

sentences.zh: 又立市於後庭，與宮人宴戲，或三日不醒。

translations.literal: He moreover set up a marketplace in the rear palace, drank and revelled with palace women; sometimes three days passed without sobering.
translations.idiomatic: He opened a bazaar inside the seraglio and roistered there with women of the palace, drunken for whole days.

sentences.zh: 聰臨上秋閣，誅其特進綦毋達，太中大夫公師彧，尚書王琰、田歆，少府陳休，左衛卜崇，大司農朱誕等，皆群閹所忌也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong ascended Shangqiu Pavilion and executed his Honourable Attendant Extraordinary-in-Attendance Qiwu Da, Imperial Household Grandee Gongshi Yu, Directors Wang Yan and Tian Xin, Household Minister Chen Xiu, Guards Commandant Bu Chong, Minister of Revenue Zhu Dan and others—all of whom were resented by the pack of eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: From Shangqiu Pavilion Liu Cong put Qiwu Da, Gongshi Yu, Wang Yan, Tian Xin, Chen Xiu, Bu Chong, Zhu Dan, and more to death—every one a man the chief eunuchs hated.

sentences.zh: 侍中卜幹泣諫聰曰：「陛下方隆武宣之化，欲使幽谷無考槃，奈何一旦先誅忠良，將何以垂之於後！

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Bu Gan weeping remonstrated with Liu Cong: ‘Your Majesty has just proclaimed the humane rule of Martial Emperor [Wu] and Exalted Emperor [Xuan]; you vow even hidden valleys shall not hear the mourning of exile—why in one morning slaughter loyal good ministers—with what legacy shall future ages judge You?
translations.idiomatic: Bu Gan pled through tears: “You vowed to revive the humane age of Emperor Wu of Han and Emperor Xuan—yet you butcher loyal counselors at dawn? What precedent does that carve for generations to come?”

sentences.zh: 昔秦愛三良而殺之，君子知其不霸。

translations.literal: Anciently Qin valued the Three Worthies yet killed them; the gentleman knows it did not conquer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Qin mourned worthy men while cutting their throats; wise contemporaries marked that no true hegemony follows such spite.

sentences.zh: 以晉厲之無道，屍三卿之後，猶有不忍之心，陛下如何忽信左右愛憎之言，欲一日屍七卿！

translations.literal: Even Jin Li lacked the Way: after corpses of three ministers, he still harboured unreadiness; why does Your Majesty suddenly trust fond-and-hateful words left and right, wishing in one day to leave seven ministers as corpses!
translations.idiomatic: Merciless Duke Li of Jin still stayed his hand after three chief ministers fell—how dare you heed chamberlain spite and butcher seven counselors at a dawn sitting!

sentences.zh: 詔尚在臣間，猶未宣露，乞垂昊天之澤，回雷霆之威。

translations.literal: The edict is still lodged among ministers, not yet promulgated; I beg august Heaven’s grace abate thunderbolt wrath.
translations.idiomatic: The writ has never left these halls—I beg skies’ mercy against your lightning temper.

sentences.zh: 且陛下直欲誅之耳，不露其罪名，何以示四海！

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty plainly means only to execute them—if You do not display their offence names, with what shall You instruct the Four Seas?
translations.idiomatic: If you intend bare murder without publishing guilt, how will you face the empire?

sentences.zh: 此豈是帝王三訊之法邪！

translations.literal: How can this match the emperor-kings’ triple-examination justice!
translations.idiomatic: Does this resemble the sovereign’s thrice-tested bar of justice?

sentences.zh: 」因叩頭流血。

translations.literal: ’ Thereupon he knocked his head bleeding.
translations.idiomatic: He beat his forehead on the stone till blood ran.

sentences.zh: 王沈叱幹曰：「卜侍中欲距詔乎？

translations.literal: Wang Shen rebuked Bu Gan: ‘Palace Attendant Bu means to obstruct the edict?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen snarled, “Bu Gan, do you refuse the command?”

sentences.zh: 」聰拂衣而入，免幹為庶人。

translations.literal: ’ Liu Cong swept his robes inward, demoting Bu Gan to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong shrugged away and cashiered Bu Gan to common cloth.

sentences.zh: 太宰劉易及大將軍劉敷、御史大夫陳元達、金紫光祿大夫王延等詣闕諫曰：「臣聞善人者，乾坤之紀，政教之本也。

translations.literal: Grand Governor Liu Yi, Grand General Liu Fu, Household Counsellor Chen Yuanda, Grand Master of Honourable Household Wang Yan, and others came to the gate and argued: ‘We have heard: good men bind heaven-and-earth norm, root of governance and doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Liu Fu, Chen Yuanda, Wang Yan and company stood shouting at the bolts: good men tether cosmos and dynasty alike.

sentences.zh: 邪佞者，宇宙之螟螣，王化之蟊賊也。

translations.literal: The crooked and fawning are the grain-borer of the universe, the millet-pest of kingly transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophants are locusts in creation’s field, borers in the king’s grain.

sentences.zh: 故文王以多士基周，桓靈以群閹亡漢，國之興亡，未有不由此也。

translations.literal: Therefore King Wen founded Zhou on many scholars; Huan and Ling destroyed Han on a swarm of palace men—a state rises or sinks; never is it not owing to this.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen built Zhou upon worthies; eunuchs broke Eastern Han—not one rise fell without such choice.

sentences.zh: 自古明王之世，未嘗有宦者與政，武、元、安、順豈足為故事乎！

translations.literal: From eldest enlightened kings’ ages, palace men participating in governance did not occur; are Martial, Yuan, An, sufficient precedent?
translations.idiomatic: Virtuous eras never surrendered government to neuters—tell me the Han anecdotes of Zhao, Yuan, An, Emperor Shun—is that dynasty’s ruin your model?

sentences.zh: 今王沈等乃處常伯之位，握生死與奪於中，勢傾海內，愛憎任之，矯弄詔旨，欺誣日月，內諂陛下，外佞相國，威權之重，侔於人主矣。

translations.literal: Presently Wang Shen and others occupy Ordinary Palace Attendant ranks, clutch life-and-death in their midst—force capsizes seas within; liking and hatred they dispense by whim; counterfeit edicts, mock sun and moon; inward they flatter Your Majesty, outward the Chancellor; prestige rivals the monarch.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen’s clique crowns itself grand secretary, dispensing death beside your pillow—they twist mandates, cloak daylight in lies, scrape to Liu Can abroad, till their glare meets the throne’s own.

sentences.zh: 王公見之駭目，卿宰望塵下車，銓衡迫之，選舉不復以實，士以屬舉，政以賄成，多樹奸徒，殘毒忠善。

translations.literal: Nobles stare in terror at them; prefects stare at carriage dust before dismounting; appointment balances are strained; nomination no longer accords merit; gentlemen bought by factions; affairs settled by bribery; many villains planted; loyal virtue cruelly tortured.
translations.idiomatic: Princes reel at sight of them; magistrates cringe in their wake. Merit lists sell to the highest rogue; nests of traitors choke the ministries while honest skins feed the knife.

sentences.zh: 知王琰等忠臣，必盡節于陛下，懼其奸萌發露，陷之極刑。

translations.literal: Knowing ministers such as Wang Yan would exhaust integrity toward Your Majesty, they dreaded their intrigue sprouting revelation, trapping them within extreme torture.
translations.idiomatic: They knew Wang Yan and like men would bleed for you alive, so they struck first lest those loyal tongues indict their plot.

sentences.zh: 陛下不垂三察，猥加誅戮，怨感穹蒼，痛入九泉，四海悲惋，賢愚傷懼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bestowed no treble examinations; casually applied slaughter—the resentful stirred the azure dome, pain sank to nine springs—four seas grieved—worthy and foolish were wounded afraid.
translations.idiomatic: You gave fair hearing neither ear nor eve; executions soured Heaven; dead and living shriek—empire mourns alike learned and blunt.

sentences.zh: 沈等皆刀鋸之餘，背恩忘義之類，豈能如士人君子感恩展效，以答乾澤也。

translations.literal: Shen and company are remnants of knife and saw, kind that betray grace—for how may they tally scholar gentlemen who feel gratitude extending efficacy answering dry-celestial favour?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen and kin are butchered husks incapable of owing true human debt—match them to gentlemen mindful of sovereign rain? Impossible.

sentences.zh: 陛下何故親近之？

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty bosom-close them?
translations.idiomatic: Why warm such vermin round your cloak?

sentences.zh: 何故貴任之？

translations.literal: Why high-entrust them?
translations.idiomatic: Why load them with honours?

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓公任易牙而亂，孝懷委黃皓而滅，此皆覆車於前，殷鑒不遠。

translations.literal: Ancient Duke Huan entrusted Yiya thus chaos; Emperor Huai set Huang Hao thus ruin—these overturned cart before; Yin’s mirror distances not.
translations.idiomatic: Qi’s Duke Huan loved Yiya to undo his line; Shu’s emperor raised Huang Hao to lose the riverlands—the rut lies fresh before your wheels.

sentences.zh: 比年地震日蝕，雨血火災，皆沈等之由。

translations.literal: Years near: earthquakes eclipse, bloodrain fire disasters—all originate with Shen cohort.
translations.idiomatic: Quakes, eclipses, blood-rain infernos—each aligns with Wang Shen’s shadow.

sentences.zh: 願陛下割翦凶醜與政之流，引尚書、御史朝省萬機，相國與公卿五日一入，會議政事，使大臣得極其言，忠臣得逞其意，則眾災自弭，和氣呈祥。

translations.literal: We petition Your Majesty excise sinister uglies interfering in governance, recall Masters of Writing and Censors palace side to reckon myriad workings; Chancellor and dukes ministers every fifth day jointly convene discourse on governance—grant great ministers full speech, loyal men full aspiration—crowding disasters self-end, consonant vapours auspicious flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Purge villains from councils; seat Masters of Writing and censors on daily seals; summon chancellor peers every five days—the honest may speak aloud, calamities dissolve, auspice returns.

sentences.zh: 今遺晉未殄，巴蜀未賓，石勒潛有跨趙魏之志，曹嶷密有王全齊之心，而復以沈等助亂大政，陛下心腹四支何處無患！

translations.literal: Now remnant Jin unslain; Ba-Shu unsubdued; Shi Le secretly bears intent pacing Zhao-Wei—Cao Yi secretly cherishes dominating-all-Qi ambitions—again Shen aids chaos in governance—Your Majesty belly-vitals four limbs—which place lacks affliction?
translations.idiomatic: Jin survives; Ba-Shu withholds tribute; Shi Le measures Zhao–Wei—Cao Yi dreams of wholly ruling Qi—with Wang Shen still poisoning policy your heart and every limb aches.

sentences.zh: 復誅巫咸，戮扁鵲，臣恐遂成桓侯膏肓之疾，後雖欲療之，其如病何！

translations.literal: Again execute Wu-healer, massacre Bian Que—your servant fears therefore Duke Huan marrow-rot affliction—even wishing later treatment—what remedy for sickness!
translations.idiomatic: Strike down every healer—you court Duke Huan’s sickness past cure; physic cannot answer rot within bone.

sentences.zh: 請免沈等官，付有司定罪。

translations.literal: We plead dismiss Shen cohort office, surrender responsible offices sentencing crime.
translations.idiomatic: Strip Wang Shen and his confederates of office and let the law try their crimes.

sentences.zh: 」聰以表示沈等，笑曰：「是兒等為元達所引，遂成癡也。

translations.literal: ’ Liu Cong showed the memorial to Wang Shen and the others and laughed: ‘Those lads were whipped up by Yuan Da [Chen Yuanda]—they have turned witless.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong handed the ministers’ plea to Wang Shen and his clique with a grin—“Yuanda coached these pups into moonstruck folly.”

sentences.zh: 」寢之。

translations.literal: ’ He shelved them.
translations.idiomatic: He filed it unheard.

sentences.zh: 沈等頓首泣曰：「臣等小人，過蒙陛下識拔，幸得備灑掃宮閣，而王公朝士疾臣等如仇讎，又深恨陛下。

translations.literal: Shen and others smashed heads crying: ‘We petty men overstayed Your Majesty discerning elevation—lucky prepared sprinkle-sweep within palace precincts—but king-dukes dawn courtiers despise our kind like foes—yet deeper hate Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen and eunuchs wailed forehead-scarlet: petty men uplifted ward your bedchamber—court lords glare venom—for that they malign you.

sentences.zh: 願收大造之恩，以臣等膏之鼎鑊，皇朝上下自然雍穆矣。

translations.literal: We beg seize great-forging mercy—render us cauldrons’ grease—imperial dynasty high-low naturally consonant revered.
translations.idiomatic: Boil us if that buys courtly peace again—we beg cauldrons’ mercy.

sentences.zh: 」聰曰：「此等狂言恆然，卿復何足恨乎！

translations.literal: ’ Liu Cong said: ‘Such wild speech ever constant—you again what suffice hate!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong said, “Courtiers rave like this every day—you need not heed them.”

sentences.zh: 」更以訪粲，粲盛稱沈等忠清，乃心王室。

translations.literal: ’ Again consulted Liu Can; Liu Can richly praised Shen pure loyalty royal household heart.
translations.idiomatic: He put the matter to Liu Can, who hailed Wang Shen and company as immaculate servants of the throne.

sentences.zh: 聰大悅，封沈為列侯。

translations.literal: Liu Cong greatly pleased, titled Wang Shen full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Pleased, Liu Cong ennobled Wang Shen full marquis.

sentences.zh: 太宰劉易詣闕，又上疏固諫。

translations.literal: Grand Governor Liu Yi again visited gate forwarding memorial steadfast remonstration.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi returned with another uncompromising petition.

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，手壞其表，易遂忿恚而死，元達哭之悲慟，曰：「人之云亡，邦國殄悴。

translations.literal: Liu Cong greatly angry hand-tore memorial; Yi then resentment-sicken died; Yuanda mourned grievous throbbing saying: ‘When men pronounce gone—state brittle-withered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong tore Liu Yi’s plea apart in rage; Yi died crushed by it. Chen Yuanda keened—noting the ode that says when worthy men disappear, kingdoms crumble.

sentences.zh: 吾既不復能言，安用此默默生乎！

translations.literal: I neither again can speak—what use this mute-living!
translations.idiomatic: If truth no longer clears my throat, why linger mute as a stump?

sentences.zh: 」歸而自殺。

translations.literal: ’ He returned home and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He went home and opened his veins.

sentences.zh: 北地饑甚，人相食啖，羌酋大軍須運糧以給麹昌，劉雅擊敗之。

translations.literal: Beidi hungered extreme; people mutually ate one another; a Qiang chieftain moved grain transports to supply Qu Chang—Liu Ya defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Beidi’s famine turned men cannibal; a Qiang chieftain ran grain trains to feed Qu Chang—Liu Ya shattered the effort.

sentences.zh: 麹允與劉曜戰于磻石谷，王師敗績，允奔靈武。

translations.literal: Qu Yun battled Liu Yao at Panshi Valley; royal armies disastrous defeat; Yun fled Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun met Liu Yao in Panshi defile; imperial lines broke; Qu Yun galloped to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 平陽大饑，流叛死亡十有五六。

translations.literal: Pingyang great famine; drift-rebel death five-or-six in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang starved; half the refugees and mutineers perished.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣石越率騎二萬，屯於并州，以懷撫叛者。

translations.literal: Shi Le dispatched Shi Yue leading twenty thousand horse encamped Bingzhou cherishing soothing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sent Shi Yue with twenty thousand riders to camp Bingzhou and coax defectors home.

sentences.zh: 聰使黃門侍郎喬詩讓勒，勒不奉命，潛結曹嶷，規為鼎峙之勢。

translations.literal: Liu Cong sent Yellow Gate Gentleman Qiao Shi reproving Shi Le; Shi Le refused command, secretly knotted Cao Yi, planning tripod-stance situation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s envoy Qiao Shi rebuked Shi Le, who ignored him, courted Cao Yi, and sought a three-power balance.

sentences.zh: 聰立上皇后樊氏，即張氏之侍婢也。

translations.literal: Liu Cong established superior empress Fan—namely Zhang’s maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong raised Empress Zhang’s handmaid to senior empress.

sentences.zh: 時四-{后}-之外，佩皇后璽綬者七人，朝廷內外無復綱紀，阿諛日進，貨賄公行，軍旅在外，饑疫相仍，後宮賞賜動至千萬。

translations.literal: At time beyond four empresses, seven persons wore empress seal-ribbons; court inside-outside no longer guideline; flattery daily advanced; bribes public walked; armies abroad; famine-plague continued; rear-palace rewards moved reaching ten million.
translations.idiomatic: Besides four titled consorts, seven women wore the empress seal; flattery and graft replaced law; troops starved abroad while the harem spent millions on whim.

sentences.zh: 劉敷屢泣言之，聰不納，怒曰：「爾欲得使汝公死乎？

translations.literal: Liu Fu repeatedly weeping spoke; Liu Cong did not accept, angered: ‘You wish obtain making your father die?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu wept again; Liu Cong snarled—“Would you kill your own father?

sentences.zh: 朝朝夕夕生來哭人！

translations.literal: Dawn-dawn dusk-dusk living come weeping people!
translations.idiomatic: Day and night you play hired mourner!”

sentences.zh: 」敷憂忿發病而死。

translations.literal: ’ Fu worry-resentment sickened died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fu died of grief and fury.

sentences.zh: 河東大蝗，唯不食黍豆。

translations.literal: Hedong great locusts; only did not eat millet beans.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts devoured Hedong yet spared millet and beans.

sentences.zh: 靳准率部人收而埋之，哭聲聞于十餘里，後乃鑽土飛出，復食黍豆。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun led clansmen gathered buried them; wailing heard ten-odd li; afterward drilled earth flew out; again ate millet beans.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun had kin bury the swarms; laments carried ten leagues—then locusts burst soil and finished the crop.

sentences.zh: 平陽饑甚，司隸部人奔于冀州二十萬戶，石越招之故也。

translations.literal: Pingyang hungered extreme; Metropolitan district people fled Jizhou two hundred thousand households—Shi Yue summoned cause.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred thousand Metropolitan households bolted to Jizhou—Shi Yue’s invitation.

sentences.zh: 犬與豕交于相國府門，又交于宮門，又交司隸、御史門。

translations.literal: Dogs with pigs coupled Chancellor gate; again coupled palace gate; again coupled Metropolitan Censor gates.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs mounted sows before chancellor hall, palace doors, and censorate alike.

sentences.zh: 有豕著進賢冠，升聰坐。

translations.literal: There was pig wearing Advanced Worthy cap ascending Liu Cong seat.
translations.idiomatic: A pig in a scholar’s cap mounted Liu Cong’s throne.

sentences.zh: 犬冠武冠，帶綬，與豕並升。

translations.literal: Dog capped martial cap belted ribbons—together with pig ascended.
translations.idiomatic: A ribboned war-cap dog joined the pig on the dais.

sentences.zh: 俄而鬥死殿上。

translations.literal: Soon fought dead on hall.
translations.idiomatic: They tore each other dead across the floor.

sentences.zh: 宿衛莫有見其入者。

translations.literal: Night guards none saw their entering.
translations.idiomatic: No sentry saw them enter.

sentences.zh: 而聰昏虐愈甚，無誡懼之心。

translations.literal: Yet Liu Cong dim cruelty ever worse—no warning-fear heart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong only grew crueller, drunk on omens.

sentences.zh: 宴群臣於光極前殿，引見其太弟乂，容貌毀悴，鬢髮蒼然，涕泣陳謝。

translations.literal: Feasted many ministers Guangji front hall; led see Grand Heir Yi—appearance wrecked haggard—temple hair grey—tears stating apology.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangji he feasted nobles, then paraded Prince Yi—wasted, grey, weeping contrition.

sentences.zh: 聰亦對之悲慟，縱酒極歡，待之如初。

translations.literal: Liu Cong likewise toward him grief-throated—indulged wine utmost joy—treated as beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong wept with him, then drank deep and welcomed him as before.

sentences.zh: 劉曜陷長安外城，湣帝使侍中宋敞送箋於曜，帝肉袒牽羊，輿櫬銜璧出降。

translations.literal: Liu Yao fell Chang’an outer wall; Emperor Min sent Palace Attendant Song Chang delivering note Liu Yao—Emperor bared flesh led sheep—coffin-cart carried jade-mouthpiece came surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao smashed Chang’an’s outer ring; Emperor Min sent Song Chang; the Son of Heaven came bare-chested with sheep, bier, and ritual jade—the full seal of defeat.

sentences.zh: 及至平陽，聰以帝為光祿大夫、懷安侯，使粲告於太廟，大赦境內，改年麟嘉。

translations.literal: Arriving Pingyang Liu Cong made Emperor Splendid Fortune Grandee Marquis Huai’an—ordered Liu Can announce Grand Temple—great amnesty borders—changed year Linjia.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingyang Liu Cong named the Jin sovereign a minor marquis, had Liu Can boast the victory at the temple, amnestied the realm, and proclaimed the Linjia era.

sentences.zh: 麹允自殺。

translations.literal: Qu Yun suicided.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun killed himself.

sentences.zh: 聰東宮四門無故自壞，後內史女人化為丈夫。

translations.literal: Liu Cong Eastern Palace four gates without cause self-ruined; rear interior-scribe woman transformed husband.
translations.idiomatic: The heir’s four gates fell uncaused; a harem woman turned man.

sentences.zh: 時聰子約死，一指猶暖，遂不殯殮。

translations.literal: Time Liu Cong son Yue died—one finger still warm—therefore not encoffined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s son Liu Yue had just died with one finger still warm, so the corpse waited unburied.

sentences.zh: 及蘇，言見元海於不周山，經五日，遂復從至昆侖山，三日而復返於不周，見諸王公卿將相死者悉在，宮室甚壯麗，號曰蒙珠離國。

translations.literal: When revived—said saw Yuanhai at Mount Buzhou—after five days—then again followed reaching Mount Kunlun—three days again returned Buzhou—saw various king-duke minister general chancellor dead all there—palace chambers very magnificent—called Mengzhuli state.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he told of Mount Buzhou where Liu Yuan waited, of five days’ march to Kunlun and back, of every dead Han noble living on in splendour in a realm named Mengzhuli.

sentences.zh: 元海謂約曰：「東北有遮須夷國，無主久，待汝父為之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai told Yue: ‘Northeast exists Zhexu Yi state—without lord long—awaits your father becoming it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan said, “Northeast holds Zhexu, kingless too long—your father must rule it.

sentences.zh: 汝父後三年當來，來後國中大亂相殺害，吾家死亡略盡，但可永明輩十數人在耳。

translations.literal: Your father after three years ought come—after coming state within great chaos mutual slaughter—our house death nearly exhausted—only Yongming generation dozen-odd remain among ears.
translations.idiomatic: He reaches you in three years; then the realm devours itself and our line perishes save a dozen Yongming kin.

sentences.zh: 汝且還，後年當來，見汝不久。

translations.literal: You for now return—after year ought come—seeing you not long.
translations.idiomatic: Return now; within a year or two we meet again.”

sentences.zh: 」約拜辭而歸，道遇一國曰猗尼渠余國，引約入宮，與約皮囊一枚，曰：「為吾遺漢皇帝。

translations.literal: ’ Yue bowed farewell returning—road met state called Yiniquyu state—led Yue inside palace—gave Yue leather bag one—said: ‘For me deliver Han emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yue bowed out, met Yiniquyu’s king, entered his hall, received a hide pouch—“Carry this to the Han Son of Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 」約辭而歸，謂約曰：「劉郎後年來必見過，當以小女相妻。

translations.literal: ’ Yue declined returning—said to Yue: ‘Lord Liu later years coming surely will visit—shall little daughter wife you.
translations.idiomatic: As he left, the king added, “Young Lord Liu, you will visit again soon—I give you my daughter.”

sentences.zh: 」約歸，置皮囊於機上。

translations.literal: Yue returned—placed leather bag on couch.
translations.idiomatic: Home, he laid the pouch on his table.

sentences.zh: 俄而蘇，使左右機上取皮囊開之，有一方白玉，題文曰：「猗尼渠余國天王敬信遮須夷國天王，歲在攝提，當相見也。

translations.literal: Soon revived—ordered attendants couch take leather bag opened—had one square white jade—inscribed text said: ‘Yiniquyu heavenly king respectfully trusts Zhexu Yi heavenly king—year in Sheti—ought meet one another.
translations.idiomatic: He woke, opened the bag: a white jade square reading that Yiniquyu’s king salutes Zhexu’s and they meet in a Sheti year.

sentences.zh: 」馳使呈聰，聰曰：「若審如此，吾不懼死也。

translations.literal: ’ Galloped messenger presented Liu Cong—Liu Cong said: ‘If truly thus—I not fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Couriers brought it; Liu Cong murmured, “If fate truly writes so, I dread death no longer.”

sentences.zh: 」及聰死，與此玉並葬焉。

translations.literal: ’ Arriving Liu Cong died—with this jade together buried.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong died they buried the tablet with him.

sentences.zh: 時東宮鬼哭；

translations.literal: Time Eastern Palace ghosts wept;
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts keened in the heir’s halls;

sentences.zh: 赤虹經天，南有一歧；

translations.literal: scarlet rainbow crossed heaven—south had one fork;
translations.idiomatic: a blood-red rainbow spanned the sky with a spur to the south;

sentences.zh: 三日並照，各有兩珥，五色甚鮮；

translations.literal: three suns together shone—each had two ear-pendants—five colours very bright;
translations.idiomatic: three suns hung together, each wearing twin haloes in violent colour;

sentences.zh: 客星曆紫宮入於天獄而滅。

translations.literal: guest star traversed Purple Palace entered celestial prison extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: a wandering star crossed the throne stars and died in the prison mansion.

sentences.zh: 太史令康相言於聰曰：「蛇虹見彌天，一歧南徹；

translations.literal: Grand Astrologist Kang Xiang spoke Liu Cong: ‘Serpent rainbow seen filling heaven—one fork south penetrating;
translations.idiomatic: Kang Xiang warned Liu Cong: “The serpent rainbow fills heaven, its branch stabbing south;

sentences.zh: 三日並照；

translations.literal: three suns together shine;
translations.idiomatic: three suns burn as one;

sentences.zh: 客星入紫宮。

translations.literal: guest star enters Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: a stray star trespasses the polar court.

sentences.zh: 此皆大異，其徵不遠也。

translations.literal: These all great prodigies—their portent not distant.
translations.idiomatic: Each mark is extreme—their fulfilment is near.”

sentences.zh: 今虹達東西者，許洛以南不可圖也。

translations.literal: Now rainbow reaching east-west—Xu-Luo south cannot be planned.
translations.idiomatic: The bow from east to west bars conquest south of Xuchang and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 一歧南徹者，李氏當仍跨巴蜀，司馬睿終據全吳之象，天下其三分乎！

translations.literal: One fork south penetrating—Li clan ought still stride Ba-Shu—Sima Rui finally occupy all Wu’s image—realm perhaps three-divided!
translations.idiomatic: The southern fork says Li Xiong keeps Ba-Shu while Sima Rui finishes Wu—empire splits three ways.”

sentences.zh: 月為胡王，皇漢雖苞括二京，龍騰九五，然世雄燕代，肇基北朔，太陰之變其在漢域乎！

translations.literal: Moon is Hu king—imperial Han although wraps two capitals—dragon ascends nine-five—yet age heroes Yan-Dai—founding base north desert—Grand Yin’s transformation perhaps lies Han domain!
translations.idiomatic: The moon denotes barbarian thrones—though Han cradles two capitals, your dynasty rose in Yan and Dai—lunar wrath falls on northern Han itself.”

sentences.zh: 漢既據中原，曆命所屬，紫宮之異，亦不在他，此之深重，胡可盡言。

translations.literal: Han already occupies Central Plain—calendar mandate lodges—Purple Palace anomaly likewise not elsewhere—this depth-heavy—how exhaustive speech!
translations.idiomatic: We hold the heartland—the mandate hangs here—so polar warnings strike us, nowhere else—a weight no tongue lifts whole.”

sentences.zh: 石勒鴟視趙魏，曹嶷狼顧東齊，鮮卑之眾星布燕代，齊、代、燕、趙皆有將大之氣。

translations.literal: Shi Le owl-viewed Zhao Wei—Cao Yi wolf-glanced eastern Qi—Xianbei multitudes star-scattered Yan Dai—Qi Dai Yan Zhao all harbour about-to-rise vapour.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le’s glare pins Zhao–Wei—Cao Yi’s neck twists toward Qi—Xianbei stud Yan and Dai—the old Qi–Dai–Yan–Zhao lands steam with destiny.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以東夏為慮，勿顧西南。

translations.literal: We plead Your Majesty take eastern Xia as anxious—ignore southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Fear first the sunrise lands, sire—do not squander thought on Shu or Wu.

sentences.zh: 吳蜀之不能北侵，猶大漢之不能南向也。

translations.literal: Wu-Shu incapacity north-invade—as great Han incapacity south-ward.
translations.idiomatic: Shu or Wu march north no more gladly than Han marches south—neither threatens the other soon.

sentences.zh: 今京師寡弱，勒眾精盛，若盡趙魏之銳，燕之突騎自上黨而來，曹嶷率三齊之眾以繼之，陛下將何以抗之？

translations.literal: Now capital few-weak, Le host elite-strong, if exhaust Zhao Wei of keen-edge, Yan of shock-cavalry from Shangdang come, Cao Yi leads Sanqi host to continue it, Your Majesty will with what resist it?
translations.idiomatic: The capital stands thin and brittle now, while Shi Le’s armies are honed and unstoppable—if every spearhead of Zhao and Wei marches forth, Yan’s mailed riders sweep down from Shangdang, and Cao Yi brings up the levies of the Three Qi behind them, Your Majesty—what shield will you raise against such a tide?

sentences.zh: 紫宮之變何必不在此乎！

translations.literal: Purple Palace of upheaval why-necessarily not-at this!
translations.idiomatic: What says the doom that once struck the Forbidden City cannot fall here—and now?

sentences.zh: 願陛下早為之所，無使兆人生心。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty early for-it make-place, not let myriad-people birth heart.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to settle the matter while there is still time—before the people begin to turn their thoughts elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能發詔，外以遠追秦皇、漢武循海之事，內為高帝圖楚之計，無不克矣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty truly can issue edict, outward with far pursue Qin Emperor Han Wu follow-sea affairs, inward make Gao Di plot Chu scheme, none not overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly issues the command—matching without the frontier the roaming might of Qin Shi Huang’s coast and Han Wu’s fleets, matching within these walls Gaozu’s stratagem against Chu—nothing will withstand you.

sentences.zh: 」聰覽之不悅。

translations.literal: " Cong viewed it not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong read the memorial—and his brow darkened.

sentences.zh: 劉粲使王平謂劉乂曰：「適奉中詔，云京師將有變，敕裹甲以備之。

translations.literal: Liu Can envoy Wang Ping say Liu Yi: "Recently received middle edict, say capital-general will-have upheaval, order wrap armour to prepare it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can sent Wang Ping to Liu Yi with this message: “I have just received a decree from court—the capital stirs toward revolt; you are commanded to buckle on armor and make ready.”

sentences.zh: 」乂以為信然，令命宮臣裹甲以居。

translations.literal: " Yi thought trustworthy-so, ordered command palace ministers wrap armour to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi took it at face value and ordered his household officers to armor themselves and remain under arms.

sentences.zh: 粲馳遣告靳准、王沈等曰：「向也王平告云東宮陰備非常，將若之何？

translations.literal: Can hurried dispatch inform Jin Zhun Wang Shen etcetera say: "Just-now Wang Ping report say Eastern Palace covertly prepare anomaly, shall what-do?
translations.idiomatic: Can galloped messengers ahead to Jin Zhun, Wang Shen, and their circle: “A moment ago Wang Ping reported that the Eastern Palace secretly readies rebellion—what are we to do?”

sentences.zh: 」准白之，聰大驚曰：「豈有此乎！

translations.literal: " Zhun declared it, Cong greatly alarmed say: "How-have this!
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun laid it before the throne—and Liu Cong reared back. “Surely such a thing cannot be!”

sentences.zh: 」王沈等同聲曰：「臣等久聞，但恐言之陛下弗信。

translations.literal: " Wang Shen etcetera together voice say: "We long heard, only fear speaking it Your Majesty not believe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen and the rest chorused at once: “We have harbored suspicion for ages—yet dreaded that Your Majesty would not credit the words.”

sentences.zh: 」於是使粲圍東宮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon envoy Can besiege Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Then he commanded Liu Can to ring the crown prince’s compound with steel.

sentences.zh: 粲遣沈、准收氐羌酋長十餘人，窮問之，皆懸首高格，燒鐵灼目，乃自誣與乂同造逆謀。

translations.literal: Can dispatch Shen Zhun seize Di Qiang chieftains ten-odd men, thoroughly interrogate them, all hang head tall rack, burn iron scorch eye, thereby self falsely-accuse together-with Yi jointly make treason plot.
translations.idiomatic: Can set Shen and Zhun upon more than ten Di and Qiang clan heads; driven past endurance on high racks—with iron brands at their eyes—they confessed whatever was put in their mouths, swearing Liu Yi drew them into treason.

sentences.zh: 聰謂沈等言曰：「而今而後，吾知卿等忠於朕也。

translations.literal: Cong to Shen etcetera speech say: "From-now-from-after, I know you-etcetera loyal to me.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong told Shen’s party: “From this hour I understand—you are steadfast in devotion to my throne.”

sentences.zh: 當念為知無不言，勿恨往日言不用也。

translations.literal: Ought cherish as know none not speak, not resent former-days speech not-used also.
translations.idiomatic: Hold fast to candor above all regret; waste no bitterness that we once turned a deaf ear to you.”

sentences.zh: 」於是誅乂素所親厚大臣及東宮官屬數十人，皆靳准及閹豎所怨也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon execute Yi plain intimate-thick great ministers together-with Eastern Palace official retinue several tens men, all Jin Zhun and eunuchs of resent.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Yi’s sworn allies among the ministers and dozens of eastern-palace officers—every soul Jin Zhun and his eunuch cabal despised—went under the sword.

sentences.zh: 廢乂為北部王，粲使准賊殺之。

translations.literal: Depose Yi as Northern-region King, Can envoy Zhun treacher kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was cashiered as King of the Northern Marches—and Can had Zhun cut him down like a thief in the dark.

sentences.zh: 坑士眾萬五千餘人，平陽街巷為之空。

translations.literal: pit soldiers multitude ten-thousand five-thousand excess people, Pingyang lanes alleys thereby empty.
translations.idiomatic: More than fifteen thousand soldiers and commons were pitched into mass graves till Pingyang’s lanes stood hollow with silence.

sentences.zh: 氏羌叛者十餘萬落，以靳准行車騎大將軍以討之。

translations.literal: Di Qiang rebels ten-odd wan settlements, appointed Jin Zhun acting grand chariot-and-cavalry general to chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred thousand households of insurgent Di and Qiang erupted; Jin Zhun was named acting Grand Commander of Chariots and Cavalry and sent against them.

sentences.zh: 時聰境內大蝗，平陽、冀、雍尤甚。

translations.literal: Time Cong borders-within great locust, Pingyang Ji Yong especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts blackened Liu Cong’s realm; Pingyang, Ji, and Yong suffered worst.

sentences.zh: 靳准討之，震其二子而死。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun chastise them, thunder his two sons and die.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Zhun rode out against the swarm, lightning struck—and both his sons fell dead beneath it.

sentences.zh: 河汾大溢，漂沒千餘家。

translations.literal: Yellow River Fen great overflow, drift-drown thousand-odd households.
translations.idiomatic: The Fen tore its banks; a thousand families vanished under the swell.

sentences.zh: 東宮災異，門閣宮殿蕩然。

translations.literal: Eastern Palace disaster-anomaly, gate-towers palace halls swept-empty.
translations.idiomatic: Fire and freak weather gutted the Eastern Palace—gates, galleries, throne halls—all smoke and emptiness.

sentences.zh: 立粲為皇太子，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: Establish Can as imperial heir, great amnesty special-death and below.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can was named heir—and a general amnesty reached every crime shy of execution.

sentences.zh: 以粲領相國、大單于，總攝朝政如前。

translations.literal: Appoint Can supervise chancellor supreme chanyu, overall grasp court administration as-before.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the crowns of Chancellor and supreme Chányú; the reins of state remained in his fist as before.

sentences.zh: 聰校獵上林，以帝行車騎將軍，戎服執戟前導，行三驅之禮。

translations.literal: Cong review-hunt Upper Grove, appointed Emperor march chariot-and-cavalry general, military dress grasp halberd front-guide, enact three-drive rite.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong reviewed the chase in the imperial hunting park—with the captive Jin emperor trotted before him as chariot-general, clad for war and brandishing a halberd, performing the ceremonial “three sided” hunt.

sentences.zh: 粲言於聰曰：「今司馬氏跨據江東，趙固、李矩同逆相濟，興兵聚眾者皆以子鄴為名，不如除之，以絕其望。

translations.literal: Can speak Cong say: "Now Sima clan straddle occupy Jiangdong, Zhao Gu Li Ju together rebellion mutual-aid, rise arms gather multitude all take son Ye as banner, better execute him, thereby cut-off its hope.
translations.idiomatic: Can whispered to his father: “The Sima cling to lands east of the Yangzi; Zhao Gu and Li Ju feed each other treason—all who hoist banners do so beneath the hostage Prince Ye’s banner. Strike him dead and you snuff their last ember.”

sentences.zh: 」聰然之。

translations.literal: " Cong assented-it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong assented—with a flick of his sleeve that sealed another life.

sentences.zh: 趙固郭默攻其河東，至於絳邑，右司隸部人盜牧馬負妻子奔之者三萬餘騎。

translations.literal: Zhao Gu Guo Mo attack its Hedong, reach-to Jiangyi, Right Metropolitan sector people steal pasture-horse burden wife-children flee it three wan-odd riders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu and Guo Mo stormed Hedong nearly to Jiangyi until more than thirty thousand riders—household dependents of Right Metropolitan herdsmen fleeing on stolen imperial mounts—rode like a tidal bore toward liberty.

sentences.zh: 騎兵將軍劉勳追討之，殺萬餘人，固、默引歸。

translations.literal: Cavalry general Liu Xun chase chastise them, kill wan-odd people, Gu Mo lead withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry-General Liu Xun harried them, left ten thousand dead, and chased Gu and Zhao back toward their trenches.

sentences.zh: 劉頡遮邀擊之，為固所敗。

translations.literal: Liu Jie bar intercept strike them, by Gu routed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jie tried to intercept on the flank—and Zhao Gu broke him utterly.

sentences.zh: 使粲及劉雅等伐趙固，次於小平津，固揚言曰：「要當生縛劉粲以贖天子。

translations.literal: Envoy Can with Liu Ya etcetera campaign Zhao Gu, halted Xiaoqing Ford, Gu boast-say: "Mandatory shall living-bind Liu Can to ransom Son-of-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Can with Liu Ya to thrash Zhao Gu, who stalled them at Xiaoping Ford shouting: “Alive or dead I’ll truss Liu Can and trade him back for my emperor!”

sentences.zh: 」聰聞而惡之。

translations.literal: " Cong heard and despised-it.
translations.idiomatic: The boast reached Liu Cong’s ear—and drew a hiss of bile.

sentences.zh: 李矩使郭默、郭誦救趙固，屯於洛汭，遣耿稚、張皮潛濟，襲粲。

translations.literal: Li Ju envoy Guo Mo Guo Song rescue Zhao Gu, garrison-at Luo mei, dispatch Geng Zhi Zhang Pi secret ford, raid Can.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju sent Guo Mo and Guo Song to relieve Zhao Gu, encamping at the Luo bend; Geng Zhi and Zhang Pi forded unseen by night—and fell upon Can’s camps.

sentences.zh: 貝丘王翼光自厘城覘之，以告粲。

translations.literal: Beiqiu King Yi Guang from Licheng spy-it, thereby inform Can.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi Guang of Beiqiu spied forth from Licheng and carried word straight to Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「征北南渡，趙固望聲逃竄，彼方憂自固，何暇來邪！

translations.literal: Can say: "North-pacifier south-crossed, Zhao Gu hears-rumor flee-hide, those just worry self-solidify, how leisure come!
translations.idiomatic: Can sneered: “The northern pacification force has marched south across the river; Zhao Gu hears a rumor and bolts—busy shoring his own walls, hardly spare to nip at my heels!”

sentences.zh: 且聞上身在此，自當不敢北視，況敢濟乎！

translations.literal: Moreover hear Sovereign-self here, surely dare-not north-glance, how-dare moreover ford!
translations.idiomatic: They know His Majesty winters here—with luck they hardly dare glance north again, far less ford the Yellow River!”

sentences.zh: 不須驚動將士也。

translations.literal: Not must alarm-move generals troops.
translations.idiomatic: No need to fray the nerves of our warriors.”

sentences.zh: 」是夜，稚等襲敗粲軍，粲奔據陽鄉，稚館穀粲壘。

translations.literal: " That night, Zhi etcetera raid defeat Can army, Can flee occupy Yangxiang, Zhi lodge-grain Can rampart.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhi smashed Can’s corps; Can fled into Yangxiang’s earthworks—and Zhi’s men quartered themselves on Can’s own granaries.

sentences.zh: 雅聞而馳還，柵於壘外，與稚相持。

translations.literal: Ya heard and gallop return, rail rampart outer, together-with Zhi stand-off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya heard the crash of steel and tore back south, throwing palisades beyond the fort—eye to eye with Zhi through the dust.

sentences.zh: 聰聞粲敗，使太尉范隆率騎赴之，稚等懼，率眾五千，突圍趨北山而南。

translations.literal: Cong heard Can defeated, envoy Grand Guardian Fan Long lead cavalry hasten-it, Zhi etcetera fear, lead host five thousand, break encirclement race North Mountain then south.
translations.idiomatic: When news of Can’s defeat reached Pingyang, Grand Guardian Fan Long spurred reinforcements east; Zhi, seeing fresh hooves thundering in, slit the cordon with five thousand men and tore south around the northern ridges.

sentences.zh: 劉勳追之，戰于河陽，稚師大敗，死者三千五百人，投河死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Liu Xun pursue them, battle at Heyang, Zhi army great defeat, dead three thousand five hundred men, cast-river dead thousand-odd men.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun hunted them down on the Heyang fields; three thousand five hundred corpses sprawled amid the barley, another thousand drowned in the shallows clawing upstream.

sentences.zh: 聰所居螽斯則百堂災，焚其子會稽王衷已下二十有一人。

translations.literal: Cong residence Zhongsi Zebai Hall calamity, burn his sons Kuaiji Wang Zhong and below twenty-one-have-one people.
translations.idiomatic: Fire swallowed the Zhongsi Zebai Hall where Liu Cong dwelt—with it twenty-one of his sons, beginning with Zhong the Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 聰聞之，自投於床，哀塞氣絕，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Cong heard-it, self throw onto bed, grief choke breath cut, long-time then revive.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached him—and he pitched onto the couch, seized by grief till breath halted; moments passed before gray life crept back into his cheeks.

sentences.zh: 平陽西明門牡自亡，霍山崩。

translations.literal: Pingyang Western Bright Gate bolt self vanish, Mount Huo collapse.
translations.idiomatic: The western bolt of Pingyang’s Bright Gate walked off its hasp of its own accord, while Mount Huo split down its spine—a land speaking in omens.

sentences.zh: 署其驃騎大將軍、濟南王劉驥為大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書，衛大將軍、齊王劉勱為大司徒。

translations.literal: Act appoint his grand master-of-flight general Jinan King Ji as grand-general director-all central-borders armies-of-affairs Recorder-of-the-Board, Guards grand-general Qi King Liu Mai as Senior Minister-of-Education.
translations.idiomatic: He named his Master of Cavalry Ji, Prince of Jinan, Commander-in-Chief over all armies and Keeper of Documents; Guards Commander Liu Mai, Prince of Qi, became Chancellor of Education.

sentences.zh: 中常侍王沈養女年十四，有妙色，聰立為左皇后。

translations.literal: Palace-regular-attendant Wang Shen foster-daughter age fourteen, have wondrous complexion, Cong establish-as Left-empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen the eunuch’s ward—fourteen, breathtaking—was raised Left Empress of the realm.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王鑒、中書監崔懿之、中書令曹恂等諫曰：「臣聞王者之立-{后}-也，將以上配乾坤之性，象二儀敷育之義，生承宗廟，母臨天下，亡配后土，執饋皇姑，必擇世德名宗，幽閒淑令，副四海之望，稱神祇之心。

translations.literal: Director Wang Jian Secretariat-supervisor Cui Yizhi Secretariat-director Cao Xun etcetera remonstrate: "We heard king's establish-empress also, intends by-above mate Qian Kun nature, emulate two-forms spread-nurture meaning, alive inherit ancestral-shrine, mother oversee-all-under-heaven, death mate rear-earth, hold-offering imperial-aunt-by-marriage, must select generation-virtue famed-clans, secluded-grace gracious-order, fulfill four-seas expectation, tally spirits-of-heaven-earth heart.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Jian, Censor Cui Yizhi, Secretariat chief Cao Xun, spoke as one: “We have read that kings choose empresses to mirror Heaven and Earth, to embody the creative pair that mothers the dynasty alive and aligns with sovereign earth in death—to serve the ancestral temple, nourish the empire, feast the royal mothers-in-law. Lineage and virtue are the sieve; modest grace must answer the longing of seas and tally the pleasure of ghosts and gods.”

sentences.zh: 是故周文造舟，姒氏以興，《關雎》之化饗，則百世之祚永。

translations.literal: Is-why Zhou Wen build boats, Si clan thereby rise Guan Ju transform feast, then hundred-age fortune long.
translations.idiomatic: Thus King Wen of Zhou’s marriage barges floated the House of Si, and once the hymn of ospreys filled the halls, blessings stretched a hundred kings deep.”

sentences.zh: 孝成任心縱欲，以婢為-{后}-，使皇統亡絕，社稷淪傾。

translations.literal: Xiao Cheng follow-heart unleash-desire, take bondmaid as empress, make imperial-line perish-cut, altar-grain inundate-collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng followed appetite and crowned a maid empress—the bloodline snapped, dynasty and altar toppled alike.”

sentences.zh: 有周之隆既如彼矣，大漢之禍又如此矣。

translations.literal: Have Zhou of glory already like that, Grand Han catastrophe again like-this.
translations.idiomatic: See how Zhou climbed so—and how mighty Han cratered likewise.”

sentences.zh: 從麟嘉以來，亂淫於色，縱沈之弟女，刑余小丑猶不可塵瓊寢，汙清廟，況其家婢邪！

translations.literal: From Linjia onward disorder licentious at color unleash Shen's younger nieces, punished-surplus petty-clown still cannot dust jade-bedroom, befoul Pure-Temple how much-more his household slave-girl!
translations.idiomatic: Since Linjia’s reign lust has undone all order—even Wang Shen’s nieces, mutilated pipsqueaks whose touch should foul neither jasper bed nor clean temple—you would stack a maid from his kitchen above them!”

sentences.zh: 六宮妃嬪皆公子公孫，奈何一旦以婢主之，何異象榱玉簀而對腐木朽楹哉！

translations.literal: Six-Palaces consorts all prince-sons grandson-noblewomen how-then overnight take bondmaid master them how-differ ivory-rafter jade-blinds face rotten-wood rotten-pillar!
translations.idiomatic: Every consort wears the pedigree of dukes’ heirs—would you enthronise a maid in a morning? Ivory beams and silk screens deserve no rotten timber for pillars!”

sentences.zh: 臣恐無福於國家也。

translations.literal: We fear no blessing toward state-household.
translations.idiomatic: We tremble—for the dynasty this is no mercy.”

sentences.zh: 」聰覽之大怒，使宣懷謂粲曰：「鑒等小子，慢侮國家，狂言自口，無復君臣上下之禮，其速考竟。

translations.literal: " Cong reviewed-it great anger, envoy Xuan Huai speak Can say: "Jian etcetera small-folk, arrogant-insult state-house mad speech from mouth, no-return ruler-subject above-below ritual, urgently investigate-to-end.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong’s eyes flamed—he commanded Xuan Huai to hiss at Can: “Whelps like Jian mock the dynasty; frenzy spills from their tongues—they forget who stands above whom. Seal their trial tonight.”

sentences.zh: 」於是收鑒等送市。

translations.literal: " Thereupon arrest Jian etcetera dispatch market.
translations.idiomatic: They were shackled toward the headsman’s block.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫王延馳將入諫，門者弗通。

translations.literal: Gold Purple Splendor Grand Counsellor Wang Yan gallop-general enter remonstrate, gatekeeper not pass-through.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Counsellor Wang Yan whipped his horse toward the gate to plead—but the porters slammed the bolt shut.

sentences.zh: 鑒等臨刑，王沈以杖叩之曰：「庸奴，復能為惡乎？

translations.literal: Jian etcetera face execution, Wang Shen with cane knock them say: "Vulgar-slave again can enact evil?
translations.idiomatic: At the scaffold Wang Shen smacked them with his staff: “Groveling curs—still venom left to bite?”

sentences.zh: 乃公何與汝事！

translations.literal: This-lord how with you affair!
translations.idiomatic: “What’s it to the likes of you what I do!”

sentences.zh: 」鑒瞋目叱之曰：「豎子！

translations.literal: " Jian glare-eye rebuke-them say: "Brat!
translations.idiomatic: Jian glared: “Boy!

sentences.zh: 使皇漢滅者，坐汝鼠輩與靳准耳，要當訴汝於先帝，取汝等於地下。

translations.literal: Make imperial Han perish ones, sit you rat-kind Jin Zhun ear mandatory shall plead you at Former-Emperor, seize you-plural at underground.
translations.idiomatic: If the dynasty of Liu falls, it rests on rodents like you—and Jin Zhun. I swear I shall haul you beneath the sod to plead before His Late Majesty!”

sentences.zh: 」懿之曰：「靳准梟聲鏡形，必為國患。

translations.literal: " Yizhi say: "Jin Zhun owl-voice mirror-form, surely becomes state scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi added: “Jin Zhun cries like an owl—his face mirrored malice—he will devour the realm.”

sentences.zh: 汝既食人，人亦當食汝。

translations.literal: You since eat men, men also ought eat you.
translations.idiomatic: You gorge on others—the mob will gorge on you.”

sentences.zh: 」皆斬之。

translations.literal: " All behead them.
translations.idiomatic: The swords fell—all three.

sentences.zh: 聰又立其中常侍宣懷養女為中皇后。

translations.literal: Cong moreover establish inner palace-regular-attendant Xuan Huai foster-girl as central-empress.
translations.idiomatic: Nor was shame sated—Cong raised Xuan Huai’s maid as Chief Empress of the palace.

sentences.zh: 鬼哭於光極殿，又哭於建始殿。

translations.literal: Ghosts cry at Guangji Hall, moreover cry Founding-begin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts keened along the corridors of Guangji Hall—then anew in Founding Inception.

sentences.zh: 雨血平陽，廣袤十里。

translations.literal: Rain blood Pingyang breadth length ten li.
translations.idiomatic: Blood rained upon Pingyang for ten li—a crimson cloak on tile and field.

sentences.zh: 時聰子約已死，至是晝見。

translations.literal: Time Cong son Yue already died, reaching this daytime appear.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yue had long been ashes—yet now walked broad daylight halls again.

sentences.zh: 聰甚惡之，謂粲曰：「吾寢疾惙頓，怪異特甚。

translations.literal: Cong greatly loathe-it speak Can say: "I lying-ill wilt-collapse portents especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong shuddered and told Liu Can: “Sickness shackles my bed—I rot by inches—and strangeness pours in thicker each dusk.”

sentences.zh: 往以約之言為妖，比累日見之，此兒必來迎吾也。

translations.literal: Past take Yue's speech as demon, lately successive days see him, this boy certainly come welcome me.
translations.idiomatic: I once called Yue’s tales sorcery—now I meet him day on day. The boy comes to fetch me.”

sentences.zh: 何圖人死定有神靈，如是，吾不悲死也。

translations.literal: How imagine man die certainly have spirit-bright like-this, I not grieve death.
translations.idiomatic: Who knew the dead keep such fire? If so—death holds no terror for me.”

sentences.zh: 今世難未夷，非諒暗之日，朝終夕殮，旬日而葬。

translations.literal: Now age turmoil not pacified, not mourning-seclusion day, morning end evening encoffin, ten-day then bury.
translations.idiomatic: The age still writhes—no season for long veiled mourning: coffin me at dusk if I fail at dawn; let ten days find me in earth.””

sentences.zh: 」徵劉曜為丞相、錄尚書，輔政，固辭乃止。

translations.literal: " Summon Liu Yao as Chancellor Recorder-of-Board auxiliary rule, adamant decline then cease.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Liu Yao as Chancellor and Keeper of Documents to steady the reins—yet he refused until the summons broke against his stubbornness.

sentences.zh: 仍以劉景為太宰，劉驥為大司馬，劉顗為太師，朱紀為太傅，呼延晏為太保，並錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Still appoint Liu Jing as Grand Steward, Ji as Commander-in-Chief, Liu Yi as Senior Tutor, Zhu Ji as Mentor, Huyan Yan as Junior Tutor concurrent Recorder-of-Board affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jing stayed Grand Steward; Ji, Commander-in-Chief; Liu Yi as Grand Mentor; Zhu Ji Mentor; Huyan Yan Protector—all sharing the Keeper’s ledger;
