sentences.zh: 范隆守尚書令、儀同三司，靳准為大司空、領司隸校尉，皆迭決尚書奏事。

translations.literal: Fan Long guard Director-of-the-Board three-precedencies peer, Zhun as Inspector-General concurrent Metropolitan-Censor Commander, all rotated decide Board petitions.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long Acting Director ranked peer to Three Dukes; Jin Zhun Grand Provisioner commanding the capital police—between them rotating judgment on petitions.

sentences.zh: ，聰死，在位九年，偽諡曰昭武皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: , Cong died, occupy throne nine years, false posthumous say Illustrious-Martial Emperor temple-name Mighty Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Liu Cong died. Nine years sat he on that borrowed throne—the court styled him Emperor Zhaowu despite the lie, temple name Mighty Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 劉粲

translations.literal: Liu Can.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 粲字士光。

translations.literal: Can courtesy-word Shiguang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, courtesy name Shiguang.

sentences.zh: 少而俊傑，才兼文武。

translations.literal: Young and hero-outstanding talent combined civil-martial.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he blazed heroic—steel and silk both bent to his will.

sentences.zh: 自為宰相，威福任情，疏遠忠賢，昵近奸佞，任性嚴刻無恩惠，距諫飾非。

translations.literal: Since become chancellor might-blessing follow whim, distant loyal worthy, cling-near crafty-flatter obey-nature stern-severe no bounty, reject-remonstrance adorn-wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Once crowned chancellor he traded favor and thunder on whim—cast the loyal abroad, curled close to parasites; harsh whim wore no cloak of mercy, and loyal words died at the gate while fault wore gold.

sentences.zh: 好興造宮室，相國之府仿像紫宮，在位無幾，作兼晝夜，饑困窮叛，死亡相繼，粲弗之恤也。

translations.literal: Fond erect-build palace-rooms, Chancellor residence imitate Purple Palace, occupy post not-many, labour join day-night starvation distress poor rebel deaths follow-each-other, Can not-it pity.
translations.idiomatic: He loved scaffolding—raised a chancellor mansion aping the Purple Palace—and though his tenure snapped short he drove labor without nightfall while hunger bred mutiny stacked corpses like cordwood—with never a shrug from Liu Can.

sentences.zh: 既嗣偽位，尊聰-{后}-靳氏為皇太后，樊氏號弘道皇后，宣氏號弘德皇后，王氏號弘孝皇后。

translations.literal: Already inherit usurped throne honour Cong later Lady Jin clan as imperial-dowager Fan clan title Grand-Way-empress Xuan clan title Grand-Virtue-empress Wang clan title Grand-Filial-empress.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne he raised Liu Cong’s widow Lady Jin to Grand Dowager, invested Lady Fan as Empress Grand Course, Lady Xuan as Empress Grand Virtue, and Lady Wang as Empress Grand Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 靳等年皆未滿二十，並國色也，粲晨夜蒸淫於內，志不在哀。

translations.literal: Jin etcetera age all not-full twenty, together kingdom-beauties, Can morning-night steaming licentiousness within will not-at mourning.
translations.idiomatic: None yet twenty—each ravishing as stormlight—and Can steamed day and night through inner chambers heedless whether the court mourned.

sentences.zh: 立其妻靳氏為皇后，子元公為太子，大赦境內，改元漢昌。

translations.literal: Establish his wife Lady Jin clan as empress son Yuangong as imperial-heir grand amnesty borders-within alter era Han Flourish.
translations.idiomatic: His own Jin consort wore the phoenix crown; Prince Yuangong the heir’s seal; empire-wide trumpets heralded Han Flourish and amnesty beneath new bells.

sentences.zh: 雨血於平陽。

translations.literal: Rain blood at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Blood again sheeted Pingyang’s skies.

sentences.zh: 靳準將有異謀，私於粲曰：「如聞諸公將欲行伊尹、霍光之事，謀先誅太保及臣，以大司馬統萬機。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun general-have different plot private to Can say: "As-heard various lords general-wish enact Yi Yin Huo Guang affair plot first execute Junior Tutor and me with Grand Marshal grasp myriad-pivots.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun nursed treason and murmured to Can: “Word says the great lords mean to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang—murder the Protector and myself first, then hand the realm to the Commander-in-Chief.”

sentences.zh: 陛下若不先之，臣恐禍之來也不晨則夕。

translations.literal: Your Majesty if not precede them, your servant fear calamity's come also not morning then evening.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not strike before dawn, I fear disaster will own dusk.”

sentences.zh: 」粲弗納。

translations.literal: " Can not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Can shut his ears.

sentences.zh: 准懼其言之不從，謂聰二靳氏曰：「今諸公侯欲廢帝，立濟南王，恐吾家無復種矣。

translations.literal: Zhun fear his speech not obey say Cong two Lady Jin clans: "Now various lords marquises wish depose Emperor establish Jinan King fear our house no-again seed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun, seeing his seed fall on stone, cornered Liu Cong’s two Jin consorts: “The lords mean to unseat the throne for the Prince of Jinan—our kin will leave no ash.”

sentences.zh: 盍言之於帝。

translations.literal: Why-not speak it to Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Whisper it in the emperor’s ear.”

sentences.zh: 」二靳承間言之。

translations.literal: " Two Jin seize interval speak-it.
translations.idiomatic: The two Ladies slithered rumor into pillow talk.

sentences.zh: 粲誅其太宰、上洛王劉景，太師、昌國公劉顗，大司馬、濟南王劉驥，大司徒、齊王劉勱等。

translations.literal: Can execute his Grand Steward Shangluo King Liu Jing Senior Tutor Changguo Duke Liu Yi Commander-in-Chief Jinan King Ji Senior Minister Qi King Liu Mai etcetera.
translations.idiomatic: Can turned steel on Grand Steward Liu Jing Prince of Shangluo, Grand Mentor Liu Yi Duke of Changguo, Commander Liu Ji Prince of Jinan, Chancellor Liu Mai Prince of Qi—and all their train.

sentences.zh: 太傅朱紀、太尉范隆出奔長安。

translations.literal: Mentor Zhu Ji Grand Guardian Fan Long exit flee Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Mentor Zhu Ji and Grand Guardian Fan Long bolted west toward Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 又誅其車騎大將軍、吳王劉逞，驥母弟也。

translations.literal: Moreover execute his chariot-cavalry grand-general Wu King Liu Cheng Ji same-mother younger-brother.
translations.idiomatic: He cut down Chariot-General Liu Cheng Prince of Wu—Ji’s own milk-brother.

sentences.zh: 粲大閱上林，謀討石勒。

translations.literal: Can grand review Upper Grove plot campaign Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Can paraded the imperial hunt-park mustering host—designs on Shi Le’s throat.

sentences.zh: 以靳准為大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Appoint Jin Zhun grand-general Recorder-of-Board affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun became Commander-in-Chief and Keeper of Documents.

sentences.zh: 粲荒耽酒色，遊宴後庭，軍國之事一決於准。

translations.literal: Can wasteland immerse wine-color roam feast rear-court army-state affairs wholly decided at Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Can drowned in cups and couches while rear gardens rang with revel—soldier’s wage and dynasty’s whim both signed by Jin Zhun’s chop.

sentences.zh: 准矯粲命，以從弟明為車騎將軍，康為衛將軍。

translations.literal: Zhun counterfeit Can order clan-younger Ming chariot-cavalry general Kang Guards general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun forged edicts naming cousins Ming commander of chariotry, Kang Guards captain.

sentences.zh: 準將作亂，以金紫光祿大夫王延耆德時望，謀之於延。

translations.literal: Zhun general-make turmoil take Gold Purple Splendor Grand Counsellor Wang Yan aged-virtue time-reputation plot it toward Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Zhun readied rebellion he courted Counsellor Wang Yan—gray pillar of esteem—and drew him into counsel.

sentences.zh: 延弗從，馳將告之，遇靳康，劫延以歸。

translations.literal: Yan not-follow gallop-general inform-it meet Jin Kang kidnap Yan to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused and spurred toward the throne to expose the plot—but Jin Kang intercepted him mid-gallop and dragged him back in chains.

sentences.zh: 准勒兵入宮，升其光極前殿，下使甲士執粲，數而殺之。

translations.literal: Zhun rein troops enter palace ascend his Guangji front hall below order armored-men seize Can enumerate then kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun drove soldiery through the gates, mounted the dais of Guangji’s forehall, and had armored fists haul Liu Can forward—each crime tallied aloud before the blade fell.

sentences.zh: 劉氏男女無少長皆斬於東市。

translations.literal: Men and women of the Liu clan, with no exemption for youth or elders, were all executed at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: Every member of the Liu family—children and elders alike—was put to death at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 發掘元海、聰墓，焚燒其宗廟。

translations.literal: They opened and dug out the tombs of Yuanhai and Cong and burned their ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: They desecrated the tombs of Liu Yuan and Liu Cong and burned down the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 鬼大哭，聲聞百里。

translations.literal: Ghosts loudly wailed; the sound was heard for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits were said to howl in grief, the uproar rumored to carry a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 准自號大將軍、漢天王，置百官，遣使稱籓于晉。

translations.literal: Zhun styled himself Grand General and Heavenly King of Han, installed the hundred officials, and sent envoys to declare himself feudatory to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun proclaimed himself grand general and king of Han, constituted a full court, and dispatched envoys to offer vassalage to Jin.

sentences.zh: 左光祿劉雅出奔西平。

translations.literal: Palace Steward of the Left Liu Ya fled outward to Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya, Left Household Grandee, fled to Xiping.

sentences.zh: 尚書北宮純、胡崧等招集晉人，保于東宮，靳康攻滅之。

translations.literal: Ministers of the Interior Beigong Chun, Hu Song, and others gathered Jin people and held fast in the Eastern Palace; Jin Kang attacked and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Beigong Chun, Hu Song, and others rallied Han Chinese, entrenched themselves in the Eastern Palace, and were overrun and destroyed by Jin Kang.

sentences.zh: 準將以王延為左光祿，延罵曰：「屠各逆奴，何不速殺我，以吾左目置西陽門，觀相國之入也，右目置建春門，觀大將軍之入也。

translations.literal: Zhun was about to take Wang Yan as Palace Steward of the Left. Yan cursed, saying, "Tuge rebel slave—why not quickly kill me? Place my left eye at the Xiyang Gate to watch the Chancellor's entry, and my right eye at the Jianchun Gate to watch the Grand General's entry.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun meant to appoint Wang Yan Left Household Grandee. Wang Yan swore at him: "You Tuge traitor—kill me at once. Hang my left eye on the Xiyang Gate to see the grand chancellor enter, and my right on the Jianchun Gate to see the grand general ride in."

sentences.zh: 」准怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Zhun, angry, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Jin Zhun had him executed.

sentences.zh: 陳元達

translations.literal: Chen Yuanda
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda

sentences.zh: 陳元達，字長宏，後部人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yuanda, courtesy name Changhong, was a man of the Rear Division.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda, courtesy name Changhong, came from the Rear Division of the confederation.

sentences.zh: 本姓高，以生月妨父，故改云陳。

translations.literal: Originally the surname was Gao; because the birth month harmed the father, therefore it was changed and called Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His birth surname was Gao; the month of his birth was deemed inauspicious for his father, so the family took the name Chen instead.

sentences.zh: 少面孤貧，常躬耕兼誦書，樂道行詠，忻忻如也。

translations.literal: In youth, orphaned and poor, he constantly personally plowed while also reciting books, taking joy in the Way and chanting as he walked, glad and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from an early age, he farmed his own fields while studying, took delight in the Way, and composed verse as he went, always quietly content.

sentences.zh: 至年四十，不與人交通。

translations.literal: Until he reached forty years, he did not associate or interact with people.
translations.idiomatic: He reached forty without entering public life or cultivating contacts.

sentences.zh: 元海之為左賢王，聞而招之，元達不答。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai was Left Virtuous King, he heard and summoned him; Yuanda did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: While Liu Yuan still held the title of Left Virtuous King, he heard of Chen Yuanda and invited him, but Chen did not answer.

sentences.zh: 及元海僭號，人謂元達曰：「往劉公相屈，君蔑而不顧，今稱號龍飛，君其懼乎？

translations.literal: When Yuanhai assumed the usurped title, someone said to Yuanda, "Formerly Lord Liu bent himself to invite you; you scorned and did not heed. Now he has taken the title and ascends as the dragon flies—are you perhaps afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yuan declared himself emperor, people said to Chen Yuanda, "Lord Liu once humbled himself to invite you, and you refused him coldly. Now that he has taken the throne, aren't you afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」元達笑曰：「是何言邪？

translations.literal: Yuanda laughed and said, "What sort of words are these?"
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda laughed. "What kind of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 彼人姿度卓犖，有籠羅宇宙之志，吾固知之久矣。

translations.literal: That man's bearing and measure are outstanding; he has the ambition to cage and net the cosmos—I have long known it.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing is remarkable, and he means to bring the world to heel—I have known that for a long time.

sentences.zh: 然往日所以不往者，以期運未至，不能無事喧喧，彼自有以亮吾矣。

translations.literal: Yet the reason I did not go in former days was that the appointed fortune had not yet arrived; I could not without cause make noisy clamor—he on his own has means to understand me.
translations.idiomatic: I stayed away because the time had not yet come; I was not about to stir up a fuss without reason. He is sure to take my measure in due course.

sentences.zh: 卿但識之，吾恐不過二三日，驛書必至。

translations.literal: You need only mark it—I fear within no more than two or three days a relay document is sure to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Mark my words: his summons will reach you by mounted courier within two or three days.

sentences.zh: 」其暮，元海果徵元達為黃門郎。

translations.literal: That evening, Yuanhai indeed summoned Yuanda as Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: That same evening Liu Yuan appointed him Gentlemen of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「君殆聖乎！

translations.literal: People said, "Sir, you are perhaps nearly a sage!"
translations.idiomatic: People exclaimed, "You must be nearly a sage!"

sentences.zh: 」既至，引見，元海曰：「卿若早來，豈為郎官而已。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was led in audience. Yuanhai said, "Had you come early, would you have been merely a gentleman-attendant?"
translations.idiomatic: When he presented himself, Liu Yuan said, "If you had joined me sooner, you would not be offered a mere gentleman rank."

sentences.zh: 」元達曰：「臣惟性之有分，盈分者顛。

translations.literal: Yuanda said, "Your servant considers that nature has its allotment; those who overflow the allotment topple.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda replied, "Each man has his proper measure; to exceed it is to court disaster."

sentences.zh: 臣若早叩天門者，恐大王賜處於九卿、納言之間，此則非臣之分，臣將何以堪之！

translations.literal: Had your servant early knocked on the Gate of Heaven, I fear the Great King would have granted placement between the Nine Ministers and the Grand Counselor—this then would not be your servant's allotment; how would your servant bear it!
translations.idiomatic: Had I answered your first summons, Your Majesty might have placed me among the Nine Ministers or among the highest counselors—offices beyond my station. How could I have sustained that burden?

sentences.zh: 是以抑情盤桓，待分而至，大王無過授之謗，小臣免招寇之禍，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Therefore I suppressed feeling and lingered, waiting for the allotment to arrive—so the Great King has no slander of over-bestowal, and the petty minister avoids the calamity of inviting envy—is that not satisfactory!
translations.idiomatic: So I held back until my proper station opened up—sparing you talk of reckless promotion and sparing myself the jealousy high office breeds. Surely that suited us both.

sentences.zh: 」元海大悅。

translations.literal: Yuanhai was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan was immensely pleased.

sentences.zh: 在位忠謇，屢進讜言，退而削草，雖子弟莫得而知也。

translations.literal: In office loyal and blunt, repeatedly advancing upright words; retiring he scraped away drafts—even sons and nephews could not obtain knowledge of them.
translations.idiomatic: In service he was loyal and outspoken, often submitting frank counsel; afterward he destroyed his drafts so that not even family members knew what he had written.

sentences.zh: 聰每謂元達曰：「卿當畏朕，反使朕畏卿乎？

translations.literal: Cong repeatedly said to Yuanda, "You ought to fear Us—do you instead make Us fear you?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong would say to him, "You should stand in awe of me—is it rather I who stands in awe of you?"

sentences.zh: 」元達叩頭謝曰：「臣聞師臣者王，友臣者霸。

translations.literal: Yuanda kowtowed and replied, "Your servant has heard: he who treats the minister as teacher is king; he who treats him as friend is hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuanda kowtowed and said, "The king who honors his advisor as a teacher will rule as true sovereign; he who befriends him will lead the hegemons."

sentences.zh: 臣誠愚暗無可采也，幸邀陛下垂齊桓納九九之義，故使微臣得盡愚忠。

translations.literal: Your servant is truly stupid and dark, nothing worth taking; fortunate to invite Your Majesty to extend the meaning of Duke Huan of Qi accepting the nine-nines—therefore letting this petty minister exhaust foolish loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and hardly worth heeding, yet I beg you to show me Duke Huan of Qi's willingness to hear the humblest counsel, so that I may offer the loyalty I have.

sentences.zh: 昔世宗遙可汲黯之奏，故能恢隆漢道；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Shizong from afar approved Ji An's memorials, therefore was able to expand and exalt the Han way;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu endorsed Ji An's blunt memorials even from a distance, and so restored the greatness of Han;

sentences.zh: 桀紂誅諫，幽厲弭謗，是以三代之亡也忽焉。

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou executed remonstrators; You and Li stopped slander—therefore the perdition of the Three Dynasties came swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou slew their critics; Kings You and Li silenced dissent—and the Three Dynasties collapsed overnight.

sentences.zh: 陛下以大聖應期，挺不世之量，能遠捐商周覆國之弊，近模孝武光漢之美，則天下幸甚，群臣知免。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with great sagehood responding to the period, upholds measure not-of-the-age; if able far to cast off the ills whereby Shang and Zhou overturned the state, near to pattern the splendor whereby Emperor Xiaowu glorified Han, then under heaven will be exceedingly fortunate and the host of ministers will know deliverance.
translations.idiomatic: You are the sage ordained for this age, with stature rarely matched in any generation. Reject from afar the ways that doomed Shang and Zhou, and take as your near model Emperor Wu's restoration of Han, and the realm will rejoice while your servants are spared ruin.

sentences.zh: 」及其死也，人盡冤之。

translations.literal: When he reached death, everyone deemed it wrongful injustice.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, everyone felt he had been cruelly wronged.
